===================  Integrity/Programme/TC-MECH-PROG-0001_MI_Written_Program_Rev1.docx
[Normal] TURNPIKE CHEMICALS LLC — LAKE CHARLES COMPLEX
[Normal] MECHANICAL INTEGRITY WRITTEN PROGRAM
[TABLE]
   | Document / Rev | TC-MECH-PROG-0001   Rev 1
   | Issue date | 03/2025
   | Site | 18500 Louisiana Highway 108, Lake Charles, LA 70669
   | Owner | Steven Lee, Engineering Manager
   | Review cycle | 3 years, or on material change to code, site scope or process safety scope
[/TABLE]
[TABLE]
   | Role | Name
   | Originator | Steven Lee, Engineering Manager
   | Checker | James Merchant, Mechanical Integrity Engineer
   | Approver | Sean Collins, Site Leader
[/TABLE]
[Normal] 1.  Purpose and scope
[Normal] This program sets out how Turnpike Chemicals LLC discharges its mechanical integrity obligations for aboveground storage tanks and associated pressure equipment at the Lake Charles complex. It states the equipment covered, the standards applied to that equipment, and the internal commitments Turnpike makes over and above the regulatory minimum.
[Normal] The program covers:
[List Bullet] All field-erected aboveground storage tanks on site.
[List Bullet] All shop-fabricated aboveground storage tanks on site, whether or not they sit inside a bund shared with field-erected assets.
[List Bullet] Associated shell nozzles, roof fittings, water draw-off arrangements and bottom-course welds.
[List Bullet] Bund structures and secondary containment insofar as they bear on tank integrity.
[Normal] Commitments in this document are auditable in their own right. Where an internal commitment is stricter than the regulatory or code minimum, the internal commitment governs.
[Normal] 2.  Roles and responsibilities
[TABLE]
   | Role | Responsibility
   | Site Leader | Approves the program and any deviation from it.
   | Engineering Manager | Owns the program. Approves categorization decisions and interval deviations.
   | Mechanical Integrity Engineer | Maintains the tank inspection program, remaining-life calculations and category assignments. Prepares the annual inspection schedule.
   | Certified Inspector | Plans, performs and certifies inspections within the scope of their held certification. Signs inspection and fitness-for-service reports.
   | NDT Technician | Performs non-destructive examination within the method(s) for which qualified. Does not certify reports.
   | Process Engineer | Notifies Engineering of every service change that may affect the applicable inspection category.
   | Mechanical Project Engineer | Delivers repairs, replacements and refurbishment scope arising from the program.
   | Engineering Administrator | Maintains the certification register and the document control file, including the revision history for this program.
[/TABLE]
[Normal] 3.  Records
[Normal] The Mechanical Integrity Engineer holds the master record for each tank. The record shall contain, at minimum:
[List Bullet] Nameplate and construction data (year built or delivered, construction code, design basis).
[List Bullet] Foundation and roof configuration.
[List Bullet] Current inspection category and the date it was last reviewed.
[List Bullet] Inspection history, including external and internal reports, UT thickness surveys and fitness-for-service assessments.
[List Bullet] Repair history and any change of service.
[List Bullet] Signature and certificate details of the certifying inspector for each report.
[Normal] Records shall be retained for the operating life of the asset and for a further ten years following removal from service.
[Normal] Inspection reports without a valid certificate number and current expiry date in the inspector signature block are not certified evidence and shall be re-issued.
[Normal] 4.  Inspection and testing
[Normal] 4.1 Inspections shall be performed to the governing in-service standard for each equipment class. For field-erected aboveground storage tanks, that standard is API 653. For all other aboveground storage tanks, the governing in-service standard shall be identified on the asset record and applied consistently through subsequent inspection cycles.
[Normal] 4.2 External and internal inspection intervals shall be set from the remaining life determined by the most recent thickness survey or the maximum interval permitted by the governing standard, whichever is shorter.
[Normal] 4.3 Inspection of diked storage
[Normal] All diked storage on the Lake Charles site shall be subject to periodic integrity inspection under this program regardless of PSM scope. 
[Normal] Where an asset falls outside the PSM covered process, the inspection basis for that asset shall be recorded on the asset record — including the in-service standard applied, the containment class relied upon and any secondary regulatory driver (for example, SPCC integrity testing under 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6)). 
[Normal] Deviations from this clause are not permitted at engineering-manager level and shall be entered on the deviation log against this document.
[Normal] 4.4  The annual inspection schedule shall list every tank on the asset register, its current category, the last external and internal inspection dates, the next scheduled dates and any interim actions arising from category or interval changes.
[Normal] 4.5 Fitness-for-service assessments shall be performed under the site FFS assessment procedure TC-MECH-PROC-0007.
[Normal] 5.  Inspection categorization
[Normal] 5.1  Every tank in scope of this program shall be assigned an inspection category on commissioning, on entry to the Turnpike asset register, and on any material change of service. Category assignments shall be reviewed at each external inspection.
[Normal] Section 5.2 — Inspection Categorization Scheme
[Normal] Category is determined by three factors taken together: the hazard of the stored product, the presence of a water phase in continuous contact with the shell, and the containment class of the location in which the tank sits. The scheme is set out below and applies to every tank in scope regardless of size, construction code or PSM scope.
[TABLE]
   | Category | Criteria | Consequence for intervals and coverage
   | Category 1 | Water phase in continuous contact with the shell during normal operation; or a stored product classified as high-hazard under the site product hazard register; or containment inadequate to hold the full tank inventory. | Shortest interval permitted by the governing in-service standard. UT thickness survey at every external inspection, with grid focus on any water-phase contact zone. Fitness-for-service basis to be refreshed at every category review.
   | Category 2 | No continuous water phase in contact with the shell; stored product moderate-hazard under the site product hazard register; product held within a bund sized for the full tank inventory. | Standard interval under the governing in-service standard. UT thickness survey at each external inspection.
   | Category 3 | Low-hazard product; no water phase in contact with the shell; full secondary containment demonstrated. | Extended interval permitted where remaining life supports it, up to the maximum allowed by the governing standard.
[/TABLE]
[Normal] Category is not a static attribute of the tank. Category shall be reassessed whenever service changes. A service change includes, without limitation:
[List Bullet] Change of product grade or product family.
[List Bullet] Change in fill rate, throughput or operating temperature that alters corrosion or fatigue exposure.
[List Bullet] Change of blend composition where the change affects corrosivity, chloride content or water-phase behavior.
[List Bullet] Change of routing that connects the tank to a new upstream or downstream service.
[Normal] The Process Engineer shall raise notice of any such change to the Mechanical Integrity Engineer within ten working days of the change being made effective. The Mechanical Integrity Engineer shall reassess the category within a further twenty working days and, where the category increases, shall adjust the inspection schedule accordingly. A change that would extend an interval shall not be applied until the reassessment is signed by the Engineering Manager.
[Normal] Category assignments for individual tanks are recorded on the asset register and on each tank's inspection record.
[Normal] 6.  Repair and change control
[Normal] 6.1  Repairs to tanks in scope shall be planned, executed and recorded under the governing in-service standard. The following shall be recorded on the tank repair record for every repair, regardless of size:
[List Bullet] Description of the defect and its location on the shell, bottom or roof.
[List Bullet] Repair method, filler metal and any post-weld heat treatment.
[List Bullet] Signature of the certified inspector who witnessed and accepted the repair.
[List Bullet] Date of repair and return-to-service date.
[Normal] Repairs recorded only in personal notes, work orders or handwritten fitter logs are not compliant records. Where such a repair is identified after the fact, the tank repair record shall be updated on discovery and the identifying document referenced.
[Normal] 6.2 Change of service and change of product shall be raised as a Management of Change (MOC) entry before implementation. Modifications carried out under a maintenance work order do not satisfy this requirement. Where an MOC gap is identified retrospectively, the change shall be entered on the MOC log at the point of discovery, with the original implementation date recorded.
[Normal] 6.3 Any change to the applicable construction or in-service code — whether by publication of a new edition or by change of site scope — shall be evaluated by the Mechanical Integrity Engineer. Any consequential impact of a new edition on the site program shall be documented by the Mechanical Integrity Engineer and presented to the Engineering Manager for a disposition decision within sixty days of the edition coming into effect.
[Normal] 6.4  All repair and change decisions that affect the inspection interval, the inspection category, or the fitness-for-service basis for a tank shall be signed by the Engineering Manager.
[Normal] 7.  Deviations
[Normal] Deviation from this program shall be raised in writing to the Engineering Manager, entered on the deviation log against this document, and — where the deviation affects a commitment made under Section 4.3 or Section 5.2 — approved by the Site Leader. Approved deviations shall carry an expiry date and shall be reviewed at each program review cycle.
[Normal] 8.  Records and revision history

   | B | 02/2025 | Draft revised following internal review | Steven Lee | James Merchant | —

[/TABLE]

MERROWFIELD INSPECTION SERVICES, LLC
        ULTRASONIC THICKNESS MEASUREMENT PROCEDURE
                                           8420 Katy Freeway, Houston, TX 77024
                                      T +1 (713) 555-0294 · merrowfield-inspection.com

  Procedure number / Rev                  MIS-UT-003 Rev 3
  Issue date                              05/12/2024
  Supersedes                              MIS-UT-003 Rev 2 (03/18/2021)
  Written by                              D. J. Tarrant, ASNT NDT Level III (UT)
  Reviewed by                             K. R. Devereaux, QA/QC Manager
  Approved by                             R. E. Merrowfield, Technical Manager

 Applicable standards: ASME BPVC Section V, Article 23 · ASTM E797/E797M · API 653, Section 6
 (in-service inspection) · Merrowfield Written Practice MIS-WP-01 Rev 4 (ASNT SNT-TC-1A basis).


 1. Scope
 This procedure governs the manual pulse-echo ultrasonic thickness measurement of ferritic and low-alloy
 steel components performed by Merrowfield Inspection Services, LLC on aboveground atmospheric and
 low-pressure storage tanks, associated piping and structural attachments. It covers:
     • Shell plate thickness surveys on field-erected and shop-fabricated tanks, courses 1 through the
     topmost course.
     • Bottom plate thickness where accessible from the shell side.
     • Nozzle neck, reinforcing pad and manway barrel thicknesses.
     • Attached piping in the range 4 in NPS and above.

 Thickness range: 0.100 in to 3.000 in on carbon and low-alloy steels of density 7.7–7.9 g/cm³ using
 contact longitudinal-wave technique. Readings outside this range require an engineering variation issued
 by the Technical Manager against this procedure.
 Materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A283, A285, A36, A516) and low-alloy steels (ASTM A387) in the as-rolled
 or normalized condition. Austenitic stainless, clad and dissimilar-metal composites are outside the scope
 of Rev 3 and are addressed under MIS-UT-004.
 Not covered: Flaw sizing, weld examination, phased-array or automated corrosion mapping. Those
 techniques are governed by separate Merrowfield procedures.


 2. Personnel qualification
 Personnel performing and interpreting ultrasonic thickness measurements under this procedure shall be
 qualified and certified in accordance with the Merrowfield Written Practice MIS-WP-01 Rev 4, which
 follows the recommended guidelines of ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2020 edition).

  Function                                    Minimum qualification
  Data acquisition (readings)                 ASNT Level II in Ultrasonic Testing (UT), current, with documented
                                              site-specific familiarization.
  Data interpretation, grid layout,           ASNT Level II in UT, current, with a minimum of 400 hours of
  reporting                                   thickness-survey experience on aboveground storage tanks.




MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                                  Page 1
   Function                                Minimum qualification
  Procedure variation, engineering        ASNT Level III in UT, current.
  review, sign-out of the deliverable

 Vision acuity shall be verified annually per ASNT SNT-TC-1A §8.2 (near-vision Jaeger J-2 at normal
 reading distance; distinguishing shades of grey on the instrument display). Certificates of qualification and
 the current vision record for each assigned technician are held in the Merrowfield personnel file and are
 available on request.
 Trainees may operate the instrument only under the direct supervision of a qualified Level II.



 3. Equipment
 3.1 Instrument
  Item                            Requirement
  Instrument type                 Digital ultrasonic thickness gauge, pulse-echo, contact mode
  Approved models                 Olympus 38DL PLUS · Olympus 27MG · GE DMS Go+ · Panametrics
                                  Magna-Mike (thin-wall verification only)
  Display resolution              0.001 in (0.01 mm) minimum
  Measurement modes               Mode 1 (interface-to-first-back-wall) for uncoated surfaces; Mode 2 with
                                  echo-to-echo for coated or lightly scaled surfaces
  Battery / operating check       Instrument self-test at start of shift; battery replaced or recharged when
                                  indicator falls below 25 %.


 3.2 Transducers
  Application                                   Transducer
  General shell (0.150 in – 1.500 in),          5 MHz dual-element, 0.434 in diameter (Olympus D790 or
  uncoated                                      equivalent)
  Thin-wall / small radius (0.100 in – 0.500    7.5 MHz dual-element, 0.283 in diameter (Olympus D791)
  in)
  Coated surfaces / echo-to-echo                5 MHz single-element with delay line (Olympus M112)
  Elevated temperature (up to 300 °F            High-temp dual-element with heat-resistant delay (Olympus
  surface)                                      D790-SM)

 Transducers exhibiting front-face wear, delamination or an inconsistent zero shall be withdrawn from
 service and returned to the calibration lab.

 3.3 Couplant
 Propylene glycol or industrial glycerin. Ultratherm-B for surface temperatures above 175 °F. Couplant
 selection shall not affect the calibrated velocity of the block used to standardize the instrument.

 3.4 Calibration blocks
  Block                                                     Purpose
  ASTM E797 five-step wedge, carbon steel, 0.100 –          Instrument standardization on thin-wall surveys
  0.500 in




MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                                  Page 2
   Block                                                     Purpose
  ASTM E797 five-step wedge, carbon steel, 0.250 –          Instrument standardization on general shell
  1.000 in
  Custom carbon-steel block, 2.000 in                       Standardization on thick sections and pad plates

 Blocks are certified annually by the Merrowfield calibration laboratory against master reference blocks
 traceable to NIST. Certificates carry a serial number that shall be recorded in the field notebook and on the
 report cover sheet.


 4. Calibration and standardization
 Instrument standardization is performed on-site immediately before survey and repeated at the following
 triggers:
     • Start of every shift, before the first reading is recorded.
     • End of every shift, before instrument shutdown, as a data-validity confirmation.
     • On any change of transducer.
     • On any change of couplant type.
     • On any change of instrument operator.
     • After any dropped or impacted instrument.
     • At intervals not exceeding four hours during continuous survey work.

 The two-point standardization is carried out on the appropriate step-wedge block at values that bracket the
 expected component thickness. The instrument is judged acceptable when the displayed thickness on
 each verification step agrees with the certified block value within ±0.002 in (±0.05 mm) or ±1 % of the
 block value, whichever is greater.
 If the check falls outside tolerance, the survey is suspended, the instrument is re-standardized, and all
 readings recorded since the last successful check are re-taken. The event is entered in the field log with
 time, block serial number and corrective action.
 Zero and velocity: Velocity is set to 0.2330 in/µs (5920 m/s) for carbon and low-alloy steel unless the
 certified block indicates otherwise; the block-derived velocity is then used. Zero is set on the transducer
 face on couplant to eliminate delay-line effects prior to standardization.


 5. Elevation Datum and Grid Convention
 5.1 Elevation datum. Elevations on all tank shell, nozzle and attached-piping readings acquired under
 this procedure are referenced to the top of the foundation ringwall. The datum is set at the intersection
 of the finished top surface of the concrete ringwall and the outside face of the tank shell, on the north side
 of the tank, and is transferred around the circumference by rotating tape or laser level. The datum is a
 property of this procedure; it is fixed by the Merrowfield technician at the time of survey and recorded on
 the survey cover sheet as “Datum: top of foundation ringwall (per Merrowfield UT Procedure Rev 3,
 Section 5).”
 5.2 Grid convention. Readings are recorded on a fixed grid of the form [course]-[quadrant]-[elevation].
 The three elements are:
     • Course — numbered from 1 at the bottom course upward (C1, C2, C3, …).
     • Quadrant — the four cardinal quadrants N, E, S, W measured clockwise from magnetic north, with
     each quadrant covering 90° of the circumference. Where a tank has a fixed cardinal reference painted
     on the shell (e.g. manway centerline), the reference is stated on the cover sheet.



MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                                  Page 3
      • Elevation — the vertical distance in inches above the datum defined in §5.1, e.g. C1-N-24in
     denotes course 1, north quadrant, 24 in above the top of the foundation ringwall.
 5.3 Number of readings. Readings are taken at four elevations per course per quadrant on the standard
 grid: 6 in, 18 in, 36 in and 60 in above datum for course 1; for upper courses, the four elevations are
 distributed at 20 %, 40 %, 60 % and 80 % of course height above the horizontal weld to the course below.
 Additional readings are added at operator discretion where visual condition indicates localized loss.
 5.4 Merrowfield UT survey workbooks. All Merrowfield ultrasonic thickness survey
 workbooks issued under this procedure, whatever the client or campaign, express grid elevations
 in inches above the top of the foundation ringwall, per the convention of §5.1 and §5.2.
 Elevations are recorded to the nearest inch and are not restated on the workbook sheets.
 The workbook does not print the datum on each sheet; the datum is defined here and inherits by
 reference from this procedure.




 5.6 Datum verification. At the start of each survey the technician shall confirm the datum, record it in the
 field notebook, and photograph the datum reference point. The photograph is included in the deliverable.




                     6. Technique
 6.1 Surface preparation
 The measurement footprint is cleaned to bare metal by wire brush, hand tool or power tool to a condition
 sufficient to obtain a consistent first-back-wall echo. Loose scale and paint are removed. Intact coating
 within manufacturer’s stated allowance for the transducer’s echo-to-echo mode may be left in place, in
 which case Mode 2 is selected.

 6.2 Reading protocol
     • Two readings are taken at each grid location, 90° apart in transducer orientation, on the same
     footprint.
     • The readings are compared. If they agree within 0.002 in, the lower value is recorded.
     • If they differ by more than 0.002 in, a third reading is taken and the lowest of the three is recorded.
     • Readings that cannot be repeated to the above rule are re-taken after re-preparation of the surface.

 6.3 Locating anomalies
 Where a recorded reading is more than 10 % below the local mean of the surrounding grid points, the
 technician shall scan a 6 in radius around the point at 1 in centers to locate the minimum. The minimum
 reading and its position (offset from grid point in the course-quadrant-elevation frame) are entered in the
 workbook.

 6.4 Elevated temperature
 Surface temperature is measured with a contact thermocouple prior to any reading. Where surface
 temperature exceeds 150 °F, high-temperature transducers and couplant are used and a temperature
 correction factor is applied per the transducer manufacturer’s data.


 7. Recording and reporting


MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                               Page 4
  7.1 Field record
 Each reading is entered directly in the field workbook (Merrowfield form F-UT-01) with:
     • Grid reference in the [course]-[quadrant]-[elevation] form (§5.2).
     • Recorded thickness in inches to three decimal places.
     • Instrument serial number, transducer serial number and calibration block serial.
     • Technician name and ASNT certificate number.
     • Date and time of reading; ambient and surface temperature.
     • Surface condition (e.g. clean bare, light scale, coated, pitted).

 7.2 Cover sheet
 The deliverable workbook carries a cover sheet stating:
     • Client, site, tank identifier, service (as supplied by client).
     • Survey date range and campaign reference.
     • Procedure reference: “Merrowfield UT Procedure Rev 3” and issue date.
     • Datum: “Top of foundation ringwall, per Section 5 of Merrowfield UT Procedure Rev 3.”
     • Instrument, transducer and block serial numbers with calibration certificate references.
     • Personnel with ASNT certificate numbers and current expiry dates.
     • Technical Manager sign-off block.

 7.3 Data deliverable
 Data are issued as an electronic workbook (.xlsx) with one worksheet per tank and one row per grid
 reading. Summary statistics per course (minimum, mean, standard deviation) are reported on a summary
 sheet.
 7.4 Certification and Level III sign-out
 The final deliverable is reviewed and signed by a Merrowfield ASNT Level III in UT before release.




 Field notebooks, cover sheets, instrument calibration records and issued workbooks are retained by
 Merrowfield for a minimum of ten years from date of issue.


 8. Health, safety and access
 Personnel shall comply with the client’s site-specific permit-to-work requirements. Working at height,
 confined-space entry, hot work permit interactions and hydrocarbon-atmosphere monitoring are governed
 by the client’s procedures and Merrowfield’s HSE plan MIS-HSE-01 Rev 6. Nothing in this procedure
 overrides those requirements.


 9. Definitions
  Term                          Definition
  Datum                         The physical reference from which all elevation readings are measured (see §5.1).
  Grid reference                The three-element locator [course]-[quadrant]-[elevation] (see §5.2).
  Standardization               The two-point instrument check against a certified block at the start of use (see §4).
  Deliverable                   The reviewed and signed workbook and cover sheet issued to the client.



MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                                      Page 5
  10. Revision history
  Rev     Date            Change                                                                     By
  1       06/22/2017      First issue.                                                               D. J. Tarrant
  2       03/18/2021      Added echo-to-echo mode for lightly coated surfaces; updated               D. J. Tarrant
                          approved transducer list; added §7.5 data retention.
  3       05/12/2024      Rewrote Section 5 to state the elevation datum explicitly as the top       D. J. Tarrant
                          of the foundation ringwall and to formalize the
                          [course]-[quadrant]-[elevation] grid convention used in Merrowfield
                          thickness-survey workbooks. Updated Level III sign-out
                          requirement. Updated approved instrument list.


 Written by: D. J. Tarrant, ASNT NDT Level III (UT), Certificate MIS-L3-UT-0007
 Reviewed by: K. R. Devereaux, QA/QC Manager
 Approved by: R. E. Merrowfield, Technical Manager

            Merrowfield Inspection Services, LLC · 8420 Katy Freeway, Houston, TX 77024 · +1 (713) 555-0294 ·
                                                merrowfield-inspection.com

ASHGROVE NDE SERVICES, LLC
       ULTRASONIC THICKNESS MEASUREMENT PROCEDURE
                                           Ashgrove NDE Services, LLC
                                    2340 Calder Avenue, Beaumont, TX 77702
                                    Tel: +1 (409) 555-0331 · ashgrove-nde.com

Procedure number / Rev               AG-UT-014 Rev 2

Issue date                           12/06/2024

Written by                           Marcus D. Rowley, ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) — Cert. No.
                                     AG-L3-0071

Reviewed by                          Priscilla A. Vandermeer, Quality Manager

Approved by                          Kenneth J. Halloran, Technical Manager

Applicable standards                 ASME BPVC Section V, Article 23 · ASTM E797 · ASTM E317 · API 653 ·
                                     Ashgrove Written Practice AG-WP-NDT-01 Rev 4



1. Scope
This procedure governs manual pulse-echo ultrasonic wall thickness measurement performed by Ashgrove
NDE Services, LLC on aboveground carbon steel welded storage tanks and their appurtenances, in the
wall-thickness range 0.100 in through 2.000 in, at metal temperatures between 30 °F and 150 °F. It covers
survey of shell courses, tank bottoms accessible from the outside face, roof plates, and nozzle necks. It does
not cover flaw sizing, phased-array corrosion mapping, or long-range guided wave, each of which is issued
under a separate Ashgrove procedure.
Surveys performed under this procedure are intended to support in-service assessment of tanks under API
653 and comparable governing standards nominated by the asset owner. The procedure produces
spot-thickness readings on a fixed grid.



2. Personnel qualification
All measurements shall be performed by an individual qualified to ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2020) Level II Ultrasonic
Testing (UT) as a minimum, holding current certification against Ashgrove Written Practice AG-WP-NDT-01.
Interpretation of readings and issue of survey deliverables shall be under the review of an individual qualified
as a UT Level III against the same written practice.




Personnel qualification records, including near-vision and color-perception acuity checks renewed annually,
are held on file at the Beaumont office and are furnished on written request.

3. Equipment and calibration

Item                        Requirement

Instrument                  Olympus 38DL PLUS or equivalent A-scan digital thickness gauge with dual-element
                            mode; resolution 0.001 in




                               AG-UT-014 Rev 2 | Ashgrove NDE Services, LLC | Page 1
 Transducer                   5 MHz dual element, 0.375 in diameter (Olympus D790 or equivalent); 2.25 MHz dual
                             for wall > 1.000 in

Couplant                     Sonotech Ultragel II or equivalent glycerine-based couplant; compatibility with
                             product certified free of chlorides and sulphides

Calibration blocks           Ashgrove step-wedge SW-CS-4 (carbon steel, 0.100–0.500 in steps of 0.050 in) and
                             SW-CS-8 (0.500–2.000 in steps of 0.100 in); ASTM E797 reference block RB-CS-1

Cable                        Coaxial, maximum 6 ft, replaced on any evidence of intermittency

Calibration shall be performed at the start of each shift, at the end of each shift, on any change of probe, on
any change of couplant type, and whenever ambient temperature has drifted more than 20 °F since the last
calibration. Calibration entries are logged on Form AG-UT-F01 and retained with the survey deliverable.
Two-point calibration is required across the range bracketing the expected wall. The instrument shall be
judged in tolerance when block readings return within ±0.003 in of the certified block value at each calibration
step. Out-of-tolerance findings void all readings taken since the previous in-tolerance calibration; affected grid
points shall be re-shot.

4. Elevation Datum and Grid Convention
4.1 Readings are taken on a fixed grid nominated on a per-tank basis in the survey Job Instruction. In the
absence of an owner-specified grid, the default is eight equally-spaced generatrix lines per course (compass
octants N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW), with readings at 6 in, 24 in, 48 in and 72 in above the datum on each
shell course of height less than 96 in, and additional stations at 96 in on any course above that height.
4.2 The elevation datum for all Ashgrove UT surveys is the bottom-of-shell weld line — that is, the outer
toe of the horizontal fillet that joins the lowest shell course to the tank bottom plate. This datum was adopted
at Rev 1 in 2019 and is retained at Rev 2 because it is a physical weld feature that can be located by
probe and steel tape at the chime without excavation, and is repeatable between crews and
between campaigns.
On Turnpike Chemicals’ field-erected tanks at Lake Charles, this datum stands 12 in (305 mm) below the top
of the foundation ringwall. The datum is established at the start of each campaign by the survey crew,
confirmed clear of coating build-up and foundation haunch detail before the first reading is taken, and
recorded on the job instruction sheet issued for that tank. The reference point is photographed for the
deliverable pack; the datum remains the physical weld feature and is not transferred from a drawing dimension.
4.3 Grid references are recorded in the form course–octant–elevation, e.g. C1-N-24in to denote a reading on
shell course 1, north generatrix, 24 inches above the bottom-of-shell weld line. Elevations are quoted in
inches above the datum.



4.4 The datum is a property of the procedure, not of the data file. Where a datum transposition is required for
owner reporting, Ashgrove issues an annotated table on request; no transposition is applied within the
workbook.


4.5 Where the bottom-of-shell weld line is obstructed (by wind-girder support brackets, insulation cladding
curb, or foundation coating), the local grid station is offset laterally along the course to the nearest clear
vertical line and the offset noted in the survey remarks column. The datum elevation is not adjusted; only the
horizontal grid coordinate moves.

5. Technique



                               AG-UT-014 Rev 2 | Ashgrove NDE Services, LLC | Page 2
 5.1 Surface preparation. Test surfaces shall be free of loose scale, paint blisters, weld spatter, and debris.
Where existing coating is thicker than 0.010 in or of unknown condition, coating is removed by hand file or
rotary flap disc to bright metal in a 1.5 in by 1.5 in square centered on the grid point. Coating removed is
recorded in the survey report to permit later touch-up by the asset owner.
5.2 Couplant. Sonotech Ultragel II (or equivalent) is applied in a continuous film between transducer face
and test surface. On vertical surfaces couplant is renewed for each reading. Product-compatibility certification
for the couplant is included in the deliverable pack.
5.3 Measurement mode and resolution. Readings are taken in dual-element mode with the transducer
barrier oriented normal to the expected corrosion grain (typically vertical on shell courses). The instrument is
set to display in inches to 0.001 in resolution. First-echo mode is used throughout; multi-echo mode is used
only for confirmation on suspect readings under 0.150 in.
5.4 Repeat readings and averaging rule. Three readings are taken within a 1 in diameter target centered on
the grid point. The minimum of the three is recorded as the reading for that grid station. Readings that vary by
more than 0.010 in between the three shots trigger a fourth confirmatory reading; where variation persists, the
target is re-examined for lamination and the finding annotated.
5.5 Temperature compensation. No temperature compensation is applied at metal temperatures between
30 °F and 150 °F, within which velocity variation in carbon steel is smaller than the instrument resolution.
Readings taken outside this range are annotated and the actual metal temperature recorded.
5.6 Areas of suspect thinning. Where a grid station returns a reading more than 20 % below its
neighboring stations, or below any owner-nominated minimum required thickness plus 0.030 in, a five-point
cluster (grid station plus four cardinal offsets at 2 in) is added and the finding annotated. Extension of scope to
a full corrosion-mapping survey is by owner instruction and is not covered by this procedure.

6. Recording and reporting
6.1 Survey data is recorded on Ashgrove Form AG-UT-F02 (thickness reading worksheet) in the field and
transposed to the electronic UT Thickness Survey Workbook (Ashgrove template WK-UT-05) at the close of
each day's work. Each electronic entry carries: grid reference (course-octant-elevation), reading in inches,
transducer probe serial number, calibration block reference, calibration timestamp, technician initials, and any
remark on surface condition.
6.2 The survey deliverable pack comprises:
  • Cover letter under Ashgrove letterhead, signed by the Technical Manager, stating the campaign dates,
    the tanks surveyed, and the procedure revision under which the work was performed.
  • The reading workbook in .xlsx form with all fields per 6.1 populated.
  • Calibration log (Form AG-UT-F01) for the campaign.
  • Certificate of personnel qualification for each technician who took readings on the campaign.
  • Photograph log of each tank showing the datum feature and any obstructions requiring lateral grid offset.
  • The current issue of this procedure.
6.3 Owners requesting workbook-only issue for internal purposes receive a cover sheet stating the
campaign dates, the tanks surveyed and the procedure revision.


6.4 Where an owner requests engineering interpretation, that work is quoted separately and issued under
Ashgrove's Engineering Assessment procedure AG-EA-002.



7. Revision history

(suspect thinning cluster). Section 6.2 pack contents expanded. Editorial pass throughout.               Halloran

 Executive Summary
 Following the acquisition of the Lake Charles site by Turnpike Chemicals LLC on 10/01/2024, Steven Lee, Engineering
 Manager, commissioned an independent re-determination of the site design wind data. The work was necessary because (a)
 the site’s previously held wind basis was prepared by the previous owner in 2023 using pre-2020 return-period data, and
 (b) revised ASCE 7 provisions and updated NOAA Gulf-of-Mexico hurricane climatology now govern.
 The study establishes a site design wind speed of 70 m/s (3-second gust at 33 ft above ground, Exposure Category C, MRI

 This study establishes the governing site design wind data for the Turnpike Chemicals Lake Charles Complex, Lake

 2. Basis and Standard
 2.1 Governing standard
 The study has been prepared in accordance with ASCE 7-22, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for
 Buildings and Other Structures, incorporating the updated hurricane wind-speed maps for the U.S. Gulf and Atlantic
 coasts published as part of the 2022 revision. Additional reference has been made to:
     • ASCE/SEI 7-22, Chapters 26 and 32, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria (2023). • API Standard 650,
     13th Edition (2020), Annex V, Design of Storage Tanks for External Pressure. • Fenwick Coastal Engineering
     FCE-TCH-2024-06, Gulf Coast Tropical-Cyclone Hazard Re-analysis, 1900–2022. • NOAA National Hurricane Center
     HURDAT2 dataset, updated through the 2023 Atlantic hurricane season, and the NOAA post-2020 Gulf-of-Mexico
     climatology re-analysis released 06/2024. • Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code, current adoption.




 2.2 Risk category
 The Lake Charles Complex is a Risk Category III facility under ASCE 7-22 Table 1.5-1. This is justified on two grounds:
     • The complex handles Class I flammable liquids at bulk quantities exceeding the PSM threshold quantities for two of
     the three storage bunds (Bunds 1 and 2).
     • Loss of integrity of primary containment during an extreme wind event would present a substantial hazard to the
     public in the surrounding parishes, including populated areas within 3 mi of the site boundary along Louisiana
     Highway 108.
 2.3 Exposure category
 Exposure Category C has been adopted for the site as a whole, in accordance with ASCE 7-22 Section 26.7. The site
 occupies open ground bordering the Calcasieu ship channel; upwind fetch in the governing hurricane sector (SSE–SW) is
 over open water and marshland, and there is no significant surface roughness that would justify Exposure B in any
 direction of interest. The more conservative Category D was considered and set aside — although portions of the upwind
 fetch are over water, the fetch across cleared but grassed marshland immediately upwind of the tank farm does not meet
 the requirement for continuous over-water exposure through the entire wind approach.
 2.4 Topographic effects
 The site is flat. Ground elevation across the tank farm ranges from +7 ft to +11 ft MSL. There are no hills, ridges or
 escarpments within the range for which ASCE 7-22 Section 26.8 requires a topographic factor greater than unity.
 Topographic factor Kzt = 1.00 across the site.
 2.5 Directionality
 Wind directionality factor Kd has been taken from ASCE 7-22 Table 26.6-1 by structure type; the study reports the basic
 wind speed only. Downstream calculations apply Kd for the specific structure being analyzed.

 4. Methodology
 4.1 Approach
 The re-determination has been carried out in three parallel strands, each treated as an independent source and then
 reconciled:
     1. ASCE 7-22 map value. Basic wind speed read from ASCE 7-22 Figure 26.5-1C (Risk Category III) at the site
     coordinates, with linear interpolation between contours.
     2. NOAA post-2020 climatology. Extreme-value analysis of tropical-cyclone maximum sustained winds within a 100
     nautical-mile radius of the site, using the HURDAT2 record from 1900 through the end of the 2023 season and
     incorporating the NOAA 06/2024 re-analysis, which increases the estimated frequency and intensity of major Gulf
     hurricanes over the post-2020 period. Return-period wind speeds were computed by generalized Pareto distribution fit
     to peaks-over-threshold, with threshold selected by the mean-residual-life method.
     3. Hindcast reconciliation. Site-specific hindcast wind speeds for the four named systems that have passed within 200
     nautical miles of the site since 2020 (Hurricanes Laura 2020, Delta 2020, Ida 2021, Francine 2024), interpolated to the
     site coordinates and used as an upper-bound check on the map value.
 The three strands are consistent within their own uncertainty bands, and the highest value has been adopted.
 4.2 Updated data set
 The 2023 study prepared by the previous owner drew on a dataset that ended prior to the 2020 Gulf hurricane season and
 quoted a lower design value. The dataset used in the present study extends that record forward by three complete hurricane
 seasons (2020–2023) and incorporates the following updates that were not available to the earlier work:

     • Hurricanes Laura (Category 4 landfall at Cameron, LA, 08/27/2020), Delta (10/09/2020), Ida (2021) and Francine
     (09/2024). • The NOAA 06/2024 Gulf-of-Mexico re-analysis, which revises upward the intensity estimates of several
     historical storms in the 1950s–1970s and increases the assessed rate of rapid intensification in the western Gulf. • ASCE
     7-22 map contours replacing the ASCE 7-16 contours used in 2023. • Revised averaging and adjustment factors for
     peak-gust reduction over the marsh–grassland fetch north of the Calcasieu channel.

 The KLCH 30-year normals produce a bimodal wind rose typical of the western Louisiana coastal plain. A field sketch

      • a primary lobe from the south to south-southeast (170°–200°) representing the dominant late-spring and

      mph and frequent gusts to 25–30 mph;
      • a secondary lobe from the north to north-northwest (340°–020°) representing the winter continental outflow
      and post-frontal regime, contributing roughly 20% of observations, with mean speeds of 10–14 mph and frequent
      gusts to 30–35 mph;

      • extreme observations dominated almost entirely by tropical cyclone passage. Non-tropical peak gusts at

 4. Extreme wind analysis
 The extreme-wind population at the Lake Charles site is dominated by tropical cyclones. Non-tropical extremes at
 KLCH do not begin to approach the design return periods relevant here. Accordingly, the site design wind speed is
 set from a hurricane simulation approach, cross-checked against the ASCE 7-16 map.

 4.1 Method
 The HURDAT2 catalogue was filtered to storms whose track passed within 200 nm of the site between 1900 and the
 close of the 2019 season. For each qualifying storm, a peak 1-minute sustained wind at the site was estimated using
 a Holland-B parametric radial profile with central pressure, radius-to-maximum-winds and translation speed drawn
 from the best-track record, adjusted to a marine 10-m surface and then converted to an Exposure C 3-second gust
 using standard averaging-time and roughness conversions.
 A Poisson-Weibull return-period model was fitted to the resulting site-peak population. Point estimates at the return
 periods of interest are summarized in Section 4.2. The fit is closed at the 2019 season; storms from the 2020 season
 onward are not incorporated.

Team,

PURPOSE
We took the site over on 10/01/2024 and inherited a large body of engineering records from Cordell Bayou — inspection reports, asset lists, drawings, calculation workbooks, MOC entries. The filenames on the share reflect their conventions, not ours. Until Leona has rebuilt the certification register and the asset register on Turnpike numbering, the inherited files stay exactly where they are, named exactly as they arrived.

DIRECTION
1. Do not rename inherited PDFs or XLSX files. Do not move them between folders. If a file needs to be referenced in a new Turnpike-authored document, cite it by its existing filename and let the new register carry the cross-reference when it is ready. Renaming as we go will fragment the audit trail and I would rather live with awkward filenames for a few months than lose traceability back to the handover.

2. New Turnpike-authored documents — anything originated by this team from today onward — follow the TC-<discipline>-<type>-<serial> scheme. Examples: TC-MECH-INSP-0142 for a mechanical inspection report, TC-MECH-PROG-0001 for a program document, TC-MECH-REG-0002 for a register. Leona will issue serials on request and maintain the master log. Do not self-allocate numbers.

ACTIONS
1. Rebuild of the inspection certification register on TC- numbering — Leona Cartwright — target 03/2025.
2. Rebuild of the tank asset register on TC- numbering — Leona Cartwright — target 03/2025.
3. Any new engineering document raised in the meantime — originator to request a TC- number from Leona before issue.

From: Steven Lee <steven.lee@turnpike-chem.com>
To: James Merchant <james.merchant@turnpike-chem.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 16:40:58 -0500
Subject: Proposed scope of the rolling program for GPSOA
Message-ID: <20260528-gpsoa-scope-001@turnpike-chem.com>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

James,

PURPOSE
Before you close out Rev B of the response plan, I want to lock the scope of the rolling inspection program we submit to GPSOA. My view is that we can properly limit it to the PSM covered process — i.e. bunds 1 and 2 — and leave bund 3 out.

BASIS
The PSM Covered Process Boundary List (TC-PROC-PSM-0003) is unambiguous that bund 3 sits below threshold quantity and is outside the PSM boundary. GPSOA's audit was framed against the PSM covered process, so a rolling program scoped to bunds 1 and 2 aligns cleanly with the boundary the regulator was working from. Six field-erected tanks in bunds 1 and 2 is the population that matters for the audit response.

DIRECTION
Please draft the rolling inspection program in the response plan on that scope. Frame it as the PSM-covered population, cite the PSM Covered Process Boundary List as the boundary reference, and describe bund 3 separately in the site inventory sections without pulling those tanks into the rolling program table itself.

RATIONALE
Cutting bund 3 out of the rolling program takes three tanks and the associated interval logic off the critical path before 08/10. Keeping the program table homogeneous makes the submission easier to read. Between the deadline pressure and the volume of work your team already has open on the bund 1 and 2 FFS work, I'd rather not carry bund 3 through the same rolling cadence unless we have to.

ACTIONS
1. Draft rolling program table on bunds 1 and 2 only — James Merchant — by 06/05/2026
2. Add a short paragraph in the plan explaining the PSM-basis scoping and cross-referencing the PSM Covered Process Boundary List — James Merchant — by 06/05/2026
3. Circulate Rev B for my mark-up before it goes to Sean — James Merchant — by 06/08/2026

If you see a reason not to run it that way, come and talk to me before you redraft. Otherwise, please proceed on that basis.

Steven

Steven Lee
Engineering Manager
Turnpike Chemicals LLC — Lake Charles

[Normal] 2.  Records transferred
[Normal] The following record sets have been physically transferred to Turnpike custody on 10/01/2024. Where a set is marked "Partial", see Section 4 for the specific gap.
[TABLE]
   | Record set | Period covered | Format | Held where | Complete?
   | External inspection reports (Bunds 1 & 2) | 2016–2023 | PDF scans and hard-copy originals | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\  | Partial — see §4
   | External inspection reports (Bund 3, shop-fabricated tanks) | 2016–2023 | PDF scans | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\Small Tanks\  | Partial — see §4
   | Ultrasonic thickness (UT) survey workbooks | 2016–2023 | XLSX and PDF | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\UT Data\  | Partial — see §4
   | Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023 | 2016–2023 | XLSX (single workbook, tank-by-tank tabs) | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\_Index\  | Complete as an index; several entries point to PDFs that were never received back from contractor
   | Fabrication / construction records — Bunds 1 & 2 | 1979–1987 (as-built) | PDF scans of nameplates, mill certs, fabricator books | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Construction\Bund 1-2\  | Complete for nameplates; fabricator books partial
   | Fabrication / construction records — Bund 3 | 2006–2011 (as-delivered) | PDF scans of nameplates, delivery notes, manufacturer certificates | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Construction\Small Tanks\  | Complete as received from manufacturer
   | Site Design Wind Data — Final — 2023 | 2023 | PDF report and calculation appendix | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Design\Wind\  | Complete as issued
   | Tank asset register (spreadsheet) | Current as of 09/2024 | XLSX | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\_Registers\  | Complete against the population.
   | MOC log (change-of-service register) | 2010–2024 | XLSX | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Process\MOC\  | Complete on its own terms.
   | Process data sheets (per tank) | Various, last revised 2019–2023 | PDF | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Process\Data Sheets\  | Complete but some pre-dates the current service (see §4)
   | Fitter repair notes (personal notebook copies) | 2015–2024 | Handwritten copies scanned to PDF | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Repairs\Chapman notes\  | Partial — informal; see §4
   | Contractor correspondence (inspection scoping, quotations, cover letters) | 2016–2024 | EML and PDF | \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Contractors\  | Contains inspection cover letters; contract terms held by Cordell Bayou legal and not transferred here
[/TABLE]
[Normal] All of the above have been copied wholesale to the Turnpike file share under whichever destination path Turnpike engineering elects. Cordell Bayou has retained a mirror copy at head office solely for the retention period required by our own record policy; no further edits will be made to that copy after the transfer date.
[Normal] 3.  Contractors and scopes
[Normal] Cordell Bayou has used five external inspection contractors at Lake Charles over the transferred period, placed campaign by campaign rather than under a standing arrangement. The incoming team should not assume that any one contractor holds UT history for the whole population.
[TABLE]
   | Contractor | Scope held | Period | Contractor procedure held on site?
   | Delta Coast Inspection Services (Lake Charles, LA) | External inspection and UT thickness surveys across Bunds 1 and 2; most recent campaigns 2020 and 2021 | 2016–2023 | No — procedure held only by the contractor; each report cites it by revision but the procedure text is not in our files
   | Bayou NDT Services / Southeast Tank Services, Inc. (and earlier, Vermilion Integrity Group; Cameron Coastal NDE) | External inspection across Bunds 1 to 3 and the wider population; occasional UT thickness scopes | 2016–2023 | No — procedures held only by the contractors
[/TABLE]
[Normal] The scopes above are as placed by Cordell Bayou; they were not a formal contract split, and campaigns were awarded individually. No inspection work has been placed at this site since 09/2024. Any contractor engaged by Turnpike after transfer will be new to the site. Reports issued over the transferred period are catalogued in the Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023.
[Normal] No contractor has transferred its internal UT procedure to Cordell Bayou custody. Each survey workbook cites the procedure by title and revision on its cover sheet. Each survey workbook cites the procedure by title and revision on its cover sheet. Turnpike may wish to request the current revision of each procedure direct from the contractor before the next cycle, as we have not previously done so.
[Normal] Contractor invoices, contract terms, and scoping correspondence outside the technical envelope are held by Cordell Bayou's contracts and procurement functions and do not form part of the engineering handover.
[Normal] 4.  Known gaps and cautions
[Normal] The following are known limitations of the transferred records. They are listed here rather than left for the incoming team to discover so that the shape of the record set is not mistaken for the shape of the asset history.
[List Bullet] Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023 is complete as a list, but not every referenced report is in the file share. The index carries a column flagging which original PDFs were not returned to Cordell Bayou by the contractor after issue. In practice this affects a small number of Bund 1 UT workbook attachments from 2019 and 2020 and one Bund 3 external inspection cover letter from 2017. The index remains the authoritative catalogue of what has been done; the physical PDFs are what is patchy.
[List Bullet] Bund 3 records were kept on a different basis to Bund 1 and Bund 2. The three shop-fabricated tanks (T-03-001, T-03-002 and T-03-003) were delivered complete to site by road between 2006 and 2011 by Southern Steel Tank Co., built to UL 142. The external inspection reports written for those tanks (2016-2023) are visual condition reports on a generic checklist.
[List Bullet] Fitter repair records are held informally. Henry Chapman has kept his repair history in personal handwritten notebooks, subsequently scanned into the fitter-notes folder. There is no formal repair record book at this site. Several minor shell and draw-off repairs across the population are captured only in Henry's notes and not on the corresponding tank inspection files. The scanned copies are complete to the best of Henry's knowledge; earlier notebooks (pre-2015) have not been located and are likely no longer in Henry's possession.
[List Bullet] Process data sheets are not all current. Where a service has changed but the modification was not routed through an MOC, the process data sheet still describes the pre-change service. Sarah Ali should be consulted before relying on any process data sheet for a service description more than three years old.
[List Bullet] The tank asset list transferred here is the Cordell Bayou working copy and carries this site’s own column layout and abbreviations. Turnpike engineering staff should verify individual field entries against primary source documents where precision is required before adopting it onto their own register.
[List Bullet] The 2023 Site Design Wind Data study is the only wind-design report in the file share.
[List Bullet] Contractor UT procedures are not on the site file share. Each contractor's survey work cites its own procedure by title and revision. The incoming team should request the applicable procedure from each contractor it engages.
[List Bullet] Personnel history transferring with the site. Sarah Ali (Process Engineer) and Henry Chapman (Mechanical Fitter) transfer to Turnpike with the site. Between them they hold the informal history of service changes and repairs that is not otherwise on paper. Neither has been asked to write that history down at handover; the fastest route to it is direct conversation.
[List Bullet] Files left uncatalogued. A number of items sit in the file share without being indexed anywhere. These include: a small folder of contractor cover letters from the 2018 UT campaign; two Bund 2 shell-thickness workbooks from 2017 that were superseded but not deleted; nameplate photographs taken for insurance purposes in 2021 that duplicate the fabrication records; and correspondence between site engineering and Cordell Bayou head office on the 2023 wind study. None of these has a formal reference number, and none was added to the Legacy Inspection Report Index. They have been left in place at handover rather than culled, on the view that Turnpike should decide what to keep before anything is discarded.
[List Bullet] No document numbering scheme in use. No inherited file carries a "TC-" prefix or any other structured document number. Titles have been assigned by authors informally, and revisions have been kept by filename convention (e.g. "…Final", "…Rev A") rather than by a controlled register. The Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023 is the closest thing to a document register that Cordell Bayou has maintained at this site, and it does not attempt to number the records it lists.
[Normal] 5.  Contacts after transfer
[Normal] The following individuals are available to answer questions on the transferred records for the periods shown. Contact details for the two transferring staff are through Turnpike's own directory from 10/01/2024. Contact for Cordell Bayou head office is via the main switchboard, +1 (713) 555-0472.
[TABLE]
   | Name | Role | Available until | For questions on
   | Sarah Ali | Process Engineer (transferring with the site) | Ongoing under Turnpike employment | Service history, process data sheets and process change notes
   | Henry Chapman | Mechanical Fitter (transferring with the site) | Ongoing under Turnpike employment | Shell and draw-off repair history and fitter notes
   | Wendell R. Prosser | Site Engineering Lead, Cordell Bayou (outgoing) | 12/31/2024 (via Cordell Bayou head office) | General handover queries, contractor scoping history, and location of any record not found in the transferred file share
   | Delta Coast Inspection Services | External inspection and UT contractor (most recent Bund 1 / Bund 2 campaigns) | Available on request; no current engagement | Its own UT procedure and workbook conventions; Bund 1 and Bund 2 survey history to 2021
   | Bayou NDT Services | External inspection contractor (2022 and 2023 campaigns) | Available on request; no current engagement | Its own procedure and workbook conventions; 2022–2023 survey history
[/TABLE]
[Normal] The record set transferred on 10/01/2024 is the entirety of what Cordell Bayou holds at this site for the mechanical integrity of the tank population. No parallel copy has been retained outside the head office archive noted above, and no further additions will be made under Cordell Bayou custody after the transfer date. Any subsequent request for clarification should be routed through Cordell Bayou head office in the first instance and Wendell R. Prosser will be reachable there through the end of 2024 for handover follow-up.
[Normal] Signed for Cordell Bayou Chemical Company, LLC:
[Normal] Wendell R. Prosser
[Normal] Site Engineering Lead — Lake Charles
[Normal] Cordell Bayou Chemical Company, LLC
[Normal] 10/01/2024

[Normal] CORDELL BAYOU CHEMICAL COMPANY, LLC
[Normal] Lake Charles Site — Site Engineering
[Normal] INTEGRITY DATA HANDOVER NOTE
[TABLE]
   | From | Wendell R. Prosser, Site Engineering Lead, Cordell Bayou Chemical Company, LLC
   | To | Steven Lee, Engineering Manager, Turnpike Chemicals LLC
   | Transfer date | 10/01/2024
   | Document ref | CB-LC-HAND-2024-01

   | Cordell Bayou HQ | 1200 Louisiana Street, Suite 4600, Houston, TX 77002

[Normal] 1.  Purpose
[Normal] This note accompanies the closing of the Lake Charles asset sale on 10/01/2024 and describes how the mechanical integrity records for the aboveground storage tank population have been maintained under Cordell Bayou. It is written for the Turnpike engineering team who will assume custody of those records at completion. The intent is to give the incoming team enough context to locate what exists, understand how it is named, and appreciate which record sets are known to be incomplete so that no gap is mistaken for a missing document that was misplaced in the handover.
[Normal] Two points frame the rest of the note. First, Cordell Bayou has never operated a formal engineering document control scheme at this site. Records were kept to the legal minimum required for our operating permits and regulatory correspondence, and files were named informally by whoever authored them. There is no site-wide document numbering scheme in use, and in particular none of the inherited files carry any "TC-" prefix, since that is Turnpike's convention rather than ours. Second, the site engineering function has run lean; the two staff transferring with the site, Sarah Ali (Process Engineer) and Henry Chapman (Mechanical Fitter), between them hold much of the informal history that has not been written down. Their working knowledge should be treated as part of the handover.
[Normal] 2.  Records transferred

7/3    T-01-001 (naphtha tk) - flange + stub

on T1-1 through the shutdown week with Delacroix.
main job was the N-3 flange face, skimmed it up
and put a new gasket in. that ones on the wo.

while the scaffold was up Ops asked for the blend
return to come in on this tank instead of dragging
the hose over from T1-2 every campaign. cut a new
4in penetration in on course 2, west side, about
3ft up off the course 1 weld. Delacroix cut it and
set the pad, I did the inside and the bolting.

- 4in sch40 A106 stub, ~9in long off the rack
- reinforcing pad cut from 3/8 plate, 10in dia.
  full fillet outside, seal weld in on the pad
- 4in 150# RF weld neck flange + gasket to suit
  the return line
- soap tested the pad tell-tale after, no leak
  off the seal weld

no separate wo raised for the stub, went on the
same permit as the flange job. R. Boudreaux had
a look before we boxed up and was happy with the
weld.

been in service since with no weep and no staining
round the pad that Ive seen going past.

materials:
  - 4in sch40 A106 stub
  - 3/8 plate pad, 10in dia
  - 4in 150# RF weld neck flange, gasket
  - E7018 rod

  1. fillet all round, wire brushed, cold
  galv on the outside afterwards.
- pressure tested local w/ water head, no weep.

while I had it open had a good look round the
bottom course under the draw-off. heavy scale
all round the inside of the shell either side
of the nozzle, came off in flakes when I
knocked it w/ the scraper. thin spots on the
bottom course near the sump - felt soft under
the hammer in two places, one about a foot off
the sump lip and one further round toward the
manway side. didn't gauge it, no UT kit on me.
told Sarah A. on shift so she knows what's
under there.

no wo raised - did it on the shift as part of
tying the change in. permit was the one already
open for the draw-off mod.

materials:
  - CS/gr spiral wound gasket, 3in class 150
  - A36 plate offcut, ~3/8 nominal, from rack
  - E7018 rod

                                       - HC
                                     H. Chapman

=================== Records/Repairs/Fitter_Notes/Fitter_Note__T02001_shell_course_1_observation.txt
18/8   T-02-001 shell course 1 - scaffold job

up on the scaffold today for the tie-in support work on the north
side. had a proper look at course 1 while I was there. more scale
on it than I would want to see, coming away in flakes where I
knocked it with the back of a wrench. underneath it isn't clean
metal - pitting across a good stretch of the course, and thin
looking with it in places. the low band by the shell to bottom weld
is the worst of it.

not what I would leave on the tank if it was up to me. the course
wants replacing before another winter on it - once the weather gets
into that pitting it will only get worse and we will be chasing it.
mentioned it to shift on the way down. no work order for the
observation itself, the scaffold job was on a separate permit.

no repair carried out today - observation only.

materials: none used for the observation. scaffold work covered
under its own permit.

                                                     - H. Chapman

=================== Records/Repairs/Fitter_Notes/Fitter_Note__T02003_access_and_staging.txt
12/9   T-02-003 shell - Ashgrove UT

went out with the Ashgrove crew first thing. they had the frame
up on the north side and were working the lower courses off it,
no problem down low. top course out of reach without additional
scaffold - the frame they brought is not tall enough to get a
probe on the top ring, and the roof edge is in the way for
lowering anything from above. they got what they could off the
ladder cage for a few grid points but it was not proper access,
more of a reach.

told the crew lead I would not sign off on the top course
readings taken like that. said we would need another lift or a
second frame section brought in if they want that elevation
covered properly. he noted it in his book. flagged it to shift
supervisor as well when I came off.

condition of what I could see from the frame - shell paint
tired on the sunny side, some flash rust round the manway
bolts, nothing I would call a defect. bottom course looked
sound at the ringwall.

no work order, no permit needed for the walk-round. Ashgrove
were on their own permit.

materials: none used.
                                                        - HC


=================== Records/Repairs/Fitter_Notes/Fitter_Note__bund_3_valve_and_coating_repairs.txt
bund 3 - small jobs through 2025
H. Chapman

--------------------------------------------------------------------

02/14   T-03-002 north side handrail post

top bolt on the handrail base plate seized off when I tried to shift
it. drilled out + tapped one size up, refitted with new stud. no other
work required. no permit - shift job.
materials: 3/8 UNC stud, 2x flat washers
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

03/12   T-03-001 outlet valve

outlet gate valve was passing when the operators tried to isolate for
the additive changeover. stripped it down - seat was pitted, gland
packing gone hard. wasn't worth reworking.
new gate valve fitted 03/2025. 2" flanged, CS body, same face-to-face
as the old one so no pipework mods. line pressure tested after.
w.o. TC-WO-2025-0184.
materials: 2" CS gate valve (stores no. VLV-GT-020-CS), new gasket
set, studs
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

04/03   T-03-003 sample tap

sample tap on the side drip line dripping. renewed the tap and put
fresh PTFE on the thread. no other issue found. shift job, no permit.
materials: 1/2" needle valve
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

05/09   T-03-001 shell coating touch-up

south face of the shell, patch about the size of a dinner plate where
the topcoat had chalked back and a bit of rust bloom coming through.
wire-brushed to sound metal, one coat primer + two coats topcoat to
spec. nothing structural, just surface. rest of the shell looks fair.
Sarah A. told, no w.o. raised.
materials: TC-approved shop primer, alkyd topcoat (grey), thinners
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

06/18   T-03-002 vent screen

bird screen on the vent had a hole in it - probably squirrel. cut off
the old screen + wired a new bit of stainless mesh in. no other work.
shift job, no permit.
materials: SS mesh offcut, tie wire
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

07/22   T-03-002 shell coating touch-up

two spots on the east side of T-03-002 where the paint had come off,
one about a hand's width and one smaller by the manway boss. same
treatment as T-03-001 back in May - wire brushed, primer + two coats
topcoat. underlying steel sound where I could see it, no measurable
thinning to touch. all above the bottom course.
no w.o. shift job. told Sarah A.
materials: shop primer, alkyd topcoat (grey)
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

08/14   T-03-003 drain plug

bottom drain plug had a slow weep at the threads. pulled it,
re-taped and put a new plug in. nothing else wrong on that side.
shift job.
materials: 3/4" BSPT plug, PTFE tape
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

09/05   T-03-001 inlet valve gland

inlet valve gland was passing a bit round the stem. new packing +
retightened gland nut. valve otherwise fine, don't need renewing yet.
shift job, no w.o.
materials: graphite packing rings
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

10/11   T-03-003 shell coating touch-up

last of the three - couple of patches on T-03-003 up near the top
course, and one spot down by the drain nozzle where I'd already
been in August. same as the other two, brushed back + primer + two
coats. small tank so didn't take long. nothing that looked deep in
the metal.
no w.o. shift job. told Sarah A.
materials: shop primer, alkyd topcoat (grey)
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

11/20   T-03-002 outlet valve stem

handwheel on the outlet valve seized on the stem - looked like it had
been over-tightened at some point + the stem was slightly bent. did
not fancy trying to force it. valve stripped, stem straightened
enough to work + new handwheel key fitted. valve now shifts by hand
as it should. body + seat looked ok, not renewing at this time.
w.o. TC-WO-2025-0511.
materials: 3/8 sq key stock, thread lock
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

12/08   T-03-001 ladder cage bolts

two of the ladder cage clamp bolts on T-03-001 had corroded through
where the cage meets the shell bracket. replaced both, cleaned up
the bracket faces + touched up the paint underneath before bolting
back. cage now solid.
shift job.
materials: 2 x M12 SS bolts, washers, primer + topcoat dab
                                                            - HC

--------------------------------------------------------------------

end of 2025 log for bund 3.
                                                            - HC

                      GULF PROCESS SAFETY AND OPERATIONS AGENCY

                               COMPLIANCE AUDIT REPORT
    Audit reference            GPSOA-2025-0417

    Site audited               Turnpike Chemicals LLC — Lake Charles Complex, 18500 Louisiana Highway 108,
                               Lake Charles, LA 70669

    Audit dates                11/18/2025 – 11/20/2025

    Lead officer               David Jeremy, Compliance Officer

    Report issued              12/02/2025

    Distribution               Sean Collins, Site Leader, Turnpike Chemicals LLC; site file; GPSOA Baton Rouge



    1. Scope of audit
    The audit examined the mechanical integrity program applied to the aboveground storage tank
    population at the Turnpike Chemicals Lake Charles Complex, with particular attention to the nine (9)
    critical tanks identified on the site's Tank Asset Register as in scope for GPSOA integrity oversight (bunds
    1, 2 and 3). The period covered was 10/01/2024 (date of site acquisition from Cordell Bayou Chemical
    Company, LLC) through the audit dates, and included inherited legacy records where these remain in
    service.
    The audit was conducted under the Gulf Process Safety and Operations Agency's compliance authority for
    process-safety asset integrity, and reviewed the site's practice against both applicable code and the
    operator's own written mechanical integrity program.

    2. Methodology
•     Document review — Tank Asset Register; Mechanical Integrity Written Program (Rev 1, 03/2025);
      Management of Change (MOC) log; inspection reports and fitness-for-service files for the nine critical
      tanks; UT thickness survey workbooks; inspection certification register; process change notes; repair
      records.
•     Site walkdown — Bunds 1, 2 and 3, including external inspection of shell, foundation, roof fittings and
      draw-off arrangements on a sample of tanks in each bund.
•     Interviews — Site Leader; Engineering Manager; Mechanical Integrity Engineer; NDT Inspector; NDT
      Technician; Process Engineer; Engineering Administrator (certification register custodian).
•     Sampling basis — All nine critical tanks reviewed at the register level. In-depth file review of a sample
      selected to cover each bund class (large field-erected, medium field-erected, small shop-fabricated) and
      each inspection contractor engaged during the review period.

    3. Findings
    Findings are stated against the applicable regulatory basis and, where relevant, against the operator's own
    written mechanical integrity program.

    4. Positive observations
• The site's Mechanical Integrity Written Program (Rev 1, 03/2025) is a substantive document that goes
beyond the minimum floor set by regulation, in particular in its treatment of inspection planning and records
control (Sections 4 and 6).


•     The 2025 external UT thickness survey campaigns on bunds 1, 2 and 3 were completed on schedule and

•     Engineering and site leadership were open with the audit team, made the requested records available,

    No imminent-danger order is issued at this time. No immediate cessation of operation is required on the
    evidence reviewed. The findings above are issued as required corrective actions with a completion date of

Subject: Findings arising from the compliance audit of 11/18/2025 – 11/20/2025
Between 11/18/2025 and 11/20/2025 the Gulf Process Safety and Operations Agency (GPSOA) conducted a
compliance audit of the mechanical integrity program applied to the aboveground storage tank population at
the Turnpike Chemicals Lake Charles Complex, with particular attention to the 9 critical tanks in bunds 1, 2 and
3 identified on the site's Tank Asset Register as in scope for GPSOA integrity oversight. The full audit findings,
methodology and enforcement position are set out in the Compliance Audit Report GPSOA-2025-0417, issued
to you separately on the date of this letter.
The audit identified four major findings (F-01 to F-04) relating to reconciliation of inspection records against
process changes; the governing in-service inspection basis recorded for the population; continuity of
API-certified sign-off; and management of change practice for tank service changes. Each finding is set out in
the audit report with its regulatory basis, required corrective action and due date, and is not repeated in full in
this letter.

No imminent-danger order is issued at this time. In arriving at that position, GPSOA has had regard to the recent
change of ownership of the site — acquisition by Turnpike Chemicals LLC from Cordell Bayou Chemical
Company, LLC on 10/01/2024 — and to the fact that a substantive written mechanical integrity program has
been issued by the operator since acquisition and that the 2025 UT thickness survey campaigns on the tanks in
scope have been completed. GPSOA's decision not to issue an imminent-danger order at this stage rests on the
expectation that the operator will complete the required corrective actions in full and on time. It is not a finding
that continued operation is unconditionally acceptable.
For continued operation of the 9 critical tanks in scope, Turnpike Chemicals LLC is required to complete
fitness-for-service assessments on those tanks, on a defensible inspection basis, and to submit to GPSOA a
rolling inspection program for the same 9 critical tanks that GPSOA can accept, by 08/10/2026. The rolling
program is to set out, for each asset, the inspection type, the governing in-service standard, the inspection
interval, the next inspection date and the API-certified
