=================== ChangeNotes/Process_Change_Note_T01001_feedstock_specification_change.eml
From: Sarah Ali <sarah.ali@turnpike-chem.com>
To: James Merchant <james.merchant@turnpike-chem.com>; Steven Lee <steven.lee@turnpike-chem.com>
Cc: Engineering Distribution <engineering@turnpike-chem.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Mar 2025 14:26:31 -0500
Subject: Process change note PCN-2025-018 - T-01-001 naphtha feedstock specification revision
Message-ID: <pcn-2025-018.t01001@turnpike-chem.com>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

All,

Recording a change to T-01-001 (straight-run naphtha feedstock storage, Spec TC-PROD-NAP-01) made on 03/17/2025.

WHAT CHANGED
The naphtha feedstock purchase specification has been tightened on two parameters:

- Total sulfur ceiling reduced from 350 wt-ppm to 150 wt-ppm.
- Reid vapor pressure (RVP) window narrowed from 8.5 - 13.5 psi to 8.5 - 11.0 psi, with the summer cap held at 10.0 psi from 05/01 to 09/30.

Deliveries received into T-01-001 from the effective date carry the revised certificate of analysis. Two supply contracts have moved to the tighter specification; the third is on the previous ceiling until the current cargo string clears, at which point the tank will hold a blend of old-spec and new-spec material until turnover.

WHY
Downstream naphtha hydrotreater catalyst life projections and the site sulfur balance both benefit from the lower sulfur ceiling; the RVP narrowing was requested by scheduling to reduce standing-loss variability on the floating roof through summer and to give a more predictable vapor space composition on receipts. Neither change was driven by tank integrity considerations.

EFFECTIVE FROM
03/17/2025 (first cargo received on new specification 03/17/2025).

EFFECT ON STORED PRODUCT PROPERTIES
While the tank inventory transitions from the previous specification to the revised specification, the following changes are expected in stored product properties and should be reflected in downstream calculations that draw on them:

- Bulk sulfur content of standing inventory falls as new-spec material displaces old-spec, with the mixing profile governed by fill/draw sequencing rather than tank turnover time.
- True vapor pressure at storage temperature reduces in line with the lower RVP window; standing-loss and working-loss estimates on the external floating roof are affected by the revised RVP range.
- Density and distillation curve envelopes tighten but remain within the range assumed by the existing process data sheet; no reissue of the density/distillation basis is required.
- No change to water content specification, water bottoms handling, or draw-off arrangement. The tank continues to receive the same feedstock family; only the specification limits move.

AFFECTED DOCUMENTS
- Purchase specification TC-PROC-SPEC-NAP-01 - reissued at Rev 4 on 03/17/2025.
- Process data sheet TC-PROC-DS-T01001 - annotation added noting the revised sulfur and RVP limits; full reissue deferred to the next scheduled revision.
- Tank service summary (the T-01-001 row in the Tank Service Summary) - specification column to be updated on the next quarterly refresh.
- Emissions inventory - standing-loss and working-loss basis for T-01-001 to be re-run at revised RVP range by the environmental team.
- Inspection plan for T-01-001 - no change proposed. James, please confirm on your side.

MOC REFERENCE
MOC-2025-011 raised 03/10/2025 and closed 03/17/2025. Risk assessment signed off by the Process Safety Coordinator; no changes to instrumentation, relief scenarios, tank fittings, or drainage arrangement.

Please cascade to your teams and let me know of any downstream documents I have missed.

Sarah

Sarah Ali
Process Engineer
Turnpike Chemicals LLC - Lake Charles Complex

Subject: Process Change =?utf-8?Q?=E2=80=94?= T-01-003 water draw-off arrangement modification
Message-ID: <20230517-t01003-drawoff@cordellbayou.com>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

All,

Recording a change to T-01-003 (gasoline blendstock, Bund 1) implemented on 05/15/2023. Please cascade to your teams and update the referenced documents at the next revision.

WHAT CHANGED

The water draw-off arrangement on T-01-003 has been modified. Two elements:

1. The water draw-off nozzle has been relocated from the original position on the lower shell to a lower elevation, tied into the floor plate area at the draw-off region. The intent is to keep the interface below normal product-out suction and to give a cleaner draw at low inventory.

2. The sampling and draw schedule has been revised. Under the previous arrangement the water leg was drawn intermittently on a per-shift check with the leg run dry between draws. Under the revised arrangement a standing water heel is retained at the draw-off region and sampled on a longer cycle (weekly grab from the sample point, monthly interface confirmation).

The practical consequence is that there is now a continuous water phase in contact with the lower shell and floor plate at the draw-off region, rather than the intermittent wetting the tank previously saw. Operations should expect the sample point to run water on every draw.

WHY

Operations raised repeated haze/water carryover findings on the blendstock rundown over Q1. Root cause was traced to the water leg drying between draws and the interface migrating above the draw-off take-off point before the next scheduled draw. Retaining a standing heel and drawing on a slower cycle from a lower take-off gives a stable interface and removes the carryover.

EFFECTIVE FROM

05/15/2023 (already in service; this note formalizes the change).

AFFECTED DOCUMENTS

- T-01-003 Process Data Sheet — service description and draw-off arrangement need reissue to reflect the standing heel and the new nozzle elevation.
- T-01-003 Operating Procedure (sampling / water draw) — revised sampling schedule to be written into the procedure.
- T-01-003 Inspection Plan — copy to Inspection for file.
- P&ID for the T-01-003 bottoms manifold — draw-off nozzle elevation and tie-in point to be redlined.

MOC REFERENCE

MOC No.: —

Please flag anything I have missed. Data sheet and procedure updates will come round for review in the next two weeks.

All,

Recording a change to T-02-002 (Bund 2, light derivative storage) commissioned on 07/16/2025.

WHAT CHANGED
The transfer line feeding T-02-002 has been debottlenecked. The 6 in header from the unit rundown to the Bund 2 manifold has been re-tied, the restriction orifice at the tie-in has been removed, and the pump discharge on P-2102 A/B has been unblocked to full curve. The maximum fill rate on T-02-002 is now 240 m3/hr, up from the previous nominal 150 m3/hr. Revised turnover time on a full tank is approximately 16 hours (previously approximately 26 hours).

Operating envelope after the change:
- Maximum fill rate: 240 m3/hr
- Nominal fill rate under normal rundown: 210 m3/hr
- Turnover time (full tank, capacity basis): ~16 hr
- Level control set-points, high/high-high alarms and vent path unchanged
- No change to product grade (TC-PROD-LGT-05) or to storage temperature

WHY
The unit rundown campaign following the Q2 turnaround increased upstream light-ends make. The old fill rate held product in the rundown surge drum longer than the drum was sized for, and we were tripping high-level on D-2101 during peak make. Debottlenecking the transfer line and running T-02-002 at the higher fill rate clears the surge drum and lets the unit stay on rate.

EFFECTIVE FROM
07/16/2025

AFFECTED DOCUMENTS
- Process data sheet for T-02-002 (TC-PROC-DS-0202) — needs reissue to reflect the revised maximum fill rate and turnover time
- Inspection plan for T-02-002 — copy to MI for file
- Operating procedure OP-2102 (T-02-002 filling and gauging) — fill rate ceiling in Section 3 to be updated to 240 m3/hr
- Overfill protection review (LOPA sheet LP-2102) — high-high response time to be re-checked against the new fill rate
- Emissions inventory sheet (Bund 2) — working losses to be recalculated at the higher turnover

MOC REFERENCE
MOC-2025-020 (raised 06/24/2025, approved 07/10/2025). Debottleneck scope and the fill rate step-up are inside the MOC boundary.

One thing I want to flag explicitly rather than leave in the small print:

1. The debottleneck raises the fill rate on T-02-002 in isolation. Nothing else on Bund 2 has been touched — T-02-001 and T-02-003 remain on their existing rundown paths.

Shout if anything on the affected-document list should move up the queue.

Sarah

Sarah Ali
Process Engineer
Turnpike Chemicals LLC — Lake Charles Complex

All,

Recording a change to T-02-003 made on 06/16/2025.

WHAT CHANGED
The derivative blend composition held in T-02-003 (Spec TC-PROD-BLD-06) has been revised to accommodate the new downstream blendstock draw. The mix ratio has been shifted as follows:

- Heavy derivative component (Stream B-14): 62% → 55% (v/v)
- Light derivative component (Stream B-22): 28% → 34% (v/v)
- Recycle cut (Stream R-07): 10% → 11% (v/v)

The revised blend is lighter overall and carries a marginally higher aromatics fraction. No new components have been introduced; only the proportion of the existing three streams has changed.

Associated operating conditions have moved accordingly:

- Blend receipt temperature: 131 °F → 118 °F (nominal), 140 °F max
- Working level operating band: 40%–75% → 45%–80%
- Recirculation pump P-2231 duty cycle: raised from 6 h/day to 9 h/day to keep the lighter blend homogeneous
- Vapor space: unchanged, remains blanketed at 15 mbar N2

Storage service classification remains derivative blend storage. No change to product family, containment or bund allocation.

WHY
The 05/2025 debottlenecking of the B-22 transfer line freed light-derivative capacity that the downstream unit can now take. Marketing requested the lighter blend to match a customer specification signed off in Q2. The lighter blend also reduces the recirculation load previously needed to hold the heavier cut in suspension over long dwell.

EFFECTIVE FROM
06/16/2025

AFFECTED DOCUMENTS
- Tank Process Data Sheet TC-PROC-DS-0203 Rev 2 — needs reissue to reflect the revised composition and the new operating band
- Blend Recipe Sheet BR-06 Rev 4 — supersedes Rev 3; issued in parallel with this note
- Tank Inspection Plan for T-02-003 (to be issued) — copy to MI for file
- Operating Procedure OP-BLD-06 Rev 5 — sections 4.2 (recipe) and 5.1 (recirculation duty) to be reissued
- Tank Service Summary — entry for T-02-003 to be updated

All,

Recording a change to T-03-002 (Bund 3 utility slop tank) implemented on 12/09/2024.

WHAT CHANGED
A new 2-in tie-in has been landed on the T-03-002 fill header, routing two additional off-spec streams into the utility slop collection:

  - C-303 stripper bottoms off-spec draw (Unit 03), and
  - F-305 filter reject / backwash return.

Both streams pass through a common manifold on the north side of the dike wall and enter T-03-002 above the existing sump-pump return. Previously T-03-002 received slop only from the unit sump pumps and from intermittent manual draining from the drum farm.

EFFECT ON CONTENTS AND OPERATING ENVELOPE
- Contents description now covers the existing aqueous / light hydrocarbon slop plus heavier stripper bottoms fractions from C-303 and filter media fines carried over from F-305. Small solids loading expected at the tank floor.
- Fill pattern moves from batch (sump-pump events, few times per shift) to near-continuous low-flow addition, with the sump-pump contribution unchanged.
- Typical operating level rises from approximately 30% to approximately 65% of working volume. High-level cut-out at 85% unchanged; low-level pump-out setpoint unchanged.
- Design pressure and design temperature unchanged. Bulk operating temperature at the shell may run 5–8 °F warmer than before due to the C-303 stream. Vent header and flame arrestor unchanged.
- No change to tank inventory limit for SPCC purposes; tank remains listed in the Bund 3 container inventory.

WHY
Debottlenecking of the C-303 / F-305 waste-handling arrangement. Prior to the tie-in, both off-spec streams were routed to drums and hauled offsite, which had become the constraint on Unit 03 throughput. Sean Collins asked engineering to route them into existing slop capacity where practicable.

EFFECTIVE FROM
12/09/2024

AFFECTED DOCUMENTS
- Process data sheet for T-03-002 (TC-PROC-DS-0032) — reissue required to reflect new streams, revised contents description and revised normal operating level.
- Inspection plan for T-03-002 (Bund 3 rolling inspection plan, current issue).
- P&IDs TC-PID-030-04 and TC-PID-030-05 — mark-ups in progress with drafting; new tie-in, manifold, isolation valves and sample point to be added.
- Bund 3 SPCC container inventory sheet (Section 6 of the SPCC plan) — contents description to be updated at next SPCC revision.
- Operator round sheet, Unit 03 — new manifold valve line-up added at position 03-N-14.

MOC REFERENCE
MOC-2024-033. Raised 12/03/2024, PHA screening completed 12/05/2024 (no new hazards flagged; existing high-level cut-out and vent path adequate), released to implementation 12/09/2024. MOC closure will follow reissue of the process data sheet.

Please pick up the affected documents at your end. James, happy to walk through the change on a call if useful.

Sarah

throughput of 600,000 metric tons per year through a single processing unit. Aboveground storage tanks hold
feedstock, intermediate streams, finished derivative products and site additives. The tank population comprises
approximately 170 aboveground storage tanks, of which nine tanks are grouped into three diked storage
areas that hold the largest inventories on site and are the subject of this Plan's container inventory (Section 2).
Ancillary tanks (drum stores, small day tanks, packaged utility tanks) are listed at Attachment A to this
Plan (TC-HSE-SPCC-0004-A) and are addressed by the site's routine visual inspection program.

1.3 General site layout
The processing unit sits at the center of the site. Diked storage areas 1, 2 and 3 lie to the north and
north-west of the processing unit and are connected to it by above-grade pipe racks. Loading racks (rail and
road) sit at the eastern boundary. Administrative and maintenance buildings are at the south-western corner.
Firewater, potable water, cooling water and sanitary utilities are consolidated in the utility area at the north-east
corner of the site.

1.4 General drainage arrangement
Site drainage is treated in detail in Section 7. In summary, storm water within the process, tank and loading
areas is collected into a segregated oily-water sewer routed to the site's API separator and biological treatment
train prior to permitted discharge. Storm water from non-oil areas (administrative parking, roadways outside
contained areas) is routed separately to the site's storm-water outfall.

1.5 Spill history
No discharges to navigable waters or adjoining shorelines meeting the reporting criteria of 40 CFR 112.4(a)
have occurred at the facility during the twelve months preceding this revision. The prior discharge history from
2016 to 2021 recorded by the previous owner is retained in the SPCC file and is not repeated here.

 and roof-to-shell joints.
 The six field-erected tanks in Bund 1 and Bund 2 — T-01-001, T-01-002, T-01-003, T-02-001, T-02-002 and

 case the annular plate radial width provided at construction is below the current-edition minimum; all six of the
 tanks lack an intermediate wind girder that the 13th Edition would today call for on the shell geometry present;

 Bund 2 tanks (T-02-001, T-02-002, T-02-003) show the widest departure from the 13th Edition set. Their small

 replacement rather than for feature-by-feature modification.
 The T-01 series is non-conforming on the same three features, but the departures are smaller as a proportion of
 the current requirement and are of a kind that could in principle be addressed by shell modification and
 localized rework. A modification study is recommended for that series in preference to replacement.

 1. Purpose and scope

 assessment is governed.
 The assessment covers the shell (all six courses) and the water draw-off nozzle assembly, and is

 Metal loss at the governing grid:
 • Governing-grid baseline thickness at 03/2014: 0.474 in

 • Metal loss at the governing grid over 11.92 yr: 0.062 in

 This is the rate reported in TC-MECH-INSP-0142 Rev 1 Section 5, computed across the full recorded
 grid record from the 03/2014 Cordell Bayou survey through the 02/2026 re-survey. Prior UT records reviewed
 by Merrowfield in support of the rate include the Cordell Bayou records CB-UT-2019-018 (04/2019) and
 CB-UT-2023-006 (04/2023) and the 04/2025 Merrowfield survey block for the remaining course 1
 quadrants.

import openpyxl, datetime as dt, statistics, json, re
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('/filesystem/Integrity/Surveys/Merrowfield_UT_Survey_2025.xlsx', data_only=True)
ws = wb['T-01-002']
CRIT = 0.225
SURVEY = dt.date(2025,4,11)      # course 1 reading date per TC-MECH-CALC-0075 Rev 1
TARGET = dt.date(2026,6,15)
BASE_YRS = 6.0                   # 04/2019 -> 04/2025 per TC-MECH-CALC-0075 convention
Y = 365.25
dt_yrs = (TARGET - SURVEY).days / Y
print("elapsed days", (TARGET-SURVEY).days, "yrs", round(dt_yrs,4))
rows = []
for r in range(10, 26):
    g = ws.cell(r,1).value
    rec = dict(grid=g, course=ws.cell(r,2).value, quad=ws.cell(r,3).value, elev=ws.cell(r,4).value,
               nom=ws.cell(r,5).value, r1=ws.cell(r,6).value, r2=ws.cell(r,7).value, rmin=ws.cell(r,8).value,
               base=ws.cell(r,9).value, bdate=ws.cell(r,10).value, surf=ws.cell(r,11).value, note=ws.cell(r,12).value)
    m = re.search(r'radius:\s*([0-9.]+)', str(rec['note']))
    rec['scan'] = float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    rows.append(rec)

def proj(t, base):
    rate = (base - t)/BASE_YRS           # in/yr
    tp = t - rate*dt_yrs
    below0 = t < CRIT
    below1 = tp < CRIT
    cross = None
    if not below0 and below1:
        tc = (t-CRIT)/rate
        cross = SURVEY + dt.timedelta(days=tc*Y)
    rl0 = None if below0 else (t-CRIT)/rate
    rl1 = None if below1 else (tp-CRIT)/rate
    nxt = None
    if not below1:
        nxt = SURVEY + dt.timedelta(days=((t-CRIT)/rate)*Y)
    return dict(rate_mpy=rate*1000, proj=tp, below0=below0, below1=below1, cross=cross, rl0=rl0, rl1=rl1, next_cross=nxt, loss=base-t)

out = {}
for basis in ('grid','scan'):
    print("\n=== BASIS", basis)
    res = []
    for rec in rows:
        t = rec['rmin'] if basis=='grid' else rec['scan']
        if t is None: continue
        p = proj(t, rec['base'])
        res.append((rec, t, p))
        print(f"{rec['grid']:8s} el{rec['elev']:>3} t={t:.3f} base={rec['base']:.3f} loss={p['loss']:.3f} rate={p['rate_mpy']:.2f} proj={p['proj']:.4f} "
              f"b0={p['below0']} b1={p['below1']} cross={p['cross']} RL0={p['rl0'] if p['rl0'] is None else round(p['rl0'],2)} RL1={p['rl1'] if p['rl1'] is None else round(p['rl1'],2)} next={p['next_cross']}")
    n0 = sum(1 for _,_,p in res if p['below0']); n1 = sum(1 for _,_,p in res if p['below1'])
    mn0 = min(res, key=lambda x: x[1]); mn1 = min(res, key=lambda x: x[2]['proj'])
    print("count below as surveyed", n0, "at target", n1)
    print("min as surveyed", mn0[0]['grid'], mn0[1], " min at target", mn1[0]['grid'], round(mn1[2]['proj'],4))

# governing-reading-per-grid basis for scan (all 16 grids: scan where recorded else grid)
print("\n=== scan-or-grid (16 grids)")
cnt0=cnt1=0
for rec in rows:
    t = rec['scan'] if rec['scan'] is not None else rec['rmin']
    p = proj(t, rec['base'])
    cnt0 += p['below0']; cnt1 += p['below1']
print(cnt0, cnt1)

# sensitivity: scan minima carried at grid-point rate
print("\n=== sensitivity: scan minima at grid rate")
for rec in rows:
    if rec['scan'] is None: continue
    rate = (rec['base']-rec['rmin'])/BASE_YRS
    t = rec['scan']; tp = t - rate*dt_yrs
    cross = None
    if t >= CRIT and tp < CRIT:
        cross = SURVEY + dt.timedelta(days=((t-CRIT)/rate)*Y)
    print(rec['grid'], t, round(rate*1000,2), round(tp,4), cross)

# course statistics
g = [r['rmin'] for r in rows]
mean = statistics.mean(g); sd = statistics.stdev(g)
print("\ncourse1 grid mean", round(mean,4), "sd", round(sd,4), "COV", round(sd/mean*100,1))
gp = [r['rmin'] - (r['base']-r['rmin'])/BASE_YRS*dt_yrs for r in rows]
print("projected mean", round(statistics.mean(gp),4))
rates = [(r['base']-r['rmin'])/BASE_YRS*1000 for r in rows]
print("grid rate range", round(min(rates),2), round(max(rates),2), "mean", round(statistics.mean(rates),2))
# nominal lifetime rate at C1-E-6
inserv = dt.date(1980,9,5)
yrs_life = (SURVEY-inserv).days/Y
print("service years", round(yrs_life,2), "C1-E-6 nominal-basis rate", round((0.5-0.202)/yrs_life*1000,2))
# indicative API 653 4.3.3.1 tmin
def tmin(H, D=92.0, G=0.96, S=23600, E=1.0, whole=True):
    h = H-1 if whole else H
    return 2.6*h*D*G/(S*E)
for H in (44,32):
    for G in (0.96,0.92):
        print("tmin H",H,"G",G, round(tmin(H,G=G),3), " S=24900:", round(tmin(H,G=G,S=24900),3))
for G in (0.96,0.92):
    Hc = 0.225*23600/(2.6*92*G)+1
    print("liquid level for tmin=0.225, G",G, round(Hc,1))
EOF

"""Appendix A data: T-01-002 course 1 readings from the Merrowfield 2025 survey workbook,
carried forward at each grid's own rate to 06/15/2026."""
import re
import datetime as dt
import statistics
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
import openpyxl

SRC = '/filesystem/Integrity/Surveys/Merrowfield_UT_Survey_2025.xlsx'
CRIT = 0.225
SURVEY = dt.date(2025, 4, 11)    # course 1 reading date, TC-MECH-CALC-0075 Rev 1
TARGET = dt.date(2026, 6, 15)
BASE_YRS = 6.0                   # 04/2019 -> 04/2025, TC-MECH-CALC-0075 Rev 1 convention
YR = 365.25
DT_YRS = (TARGET - SURVEY).days / YR


def r(x, nd):
    """Round half-up to nd decimals and return a string."""
    q = Decimal(1).scaleb(-nd)
    return str(Decimal(repr(x)).quantize(q, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def d(date):
    return date.strftime('%m/%d/%Y')


def load_rows():
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(SRC, data_only=True)
    ws = wb['T-01-002']
    rows = []
    for i in range(10, 26):
        note = str(ws.cell(i, 12).value)
        m = re.search(r'radius:\s*([0-9.]+)', note)
        rows.append(dict(
            grid=ws.cell(i, 1).value, quad=ws.cell(i, 3).value, elev=ws.cell(i, 4).value,
            r1=ws.cell(i, 6).value, r2=ws.cell(i, 7).value, rmin=ws.cell(i, 8).value,
            base=ws.cell(i, 9).value, bdate=ws.cell(i, 10).value, surf=ws.cell(i, 11).value,
            scan=float(m.group(1)) if m else None, note=note))
    return rows


def carry(t, base):
    rate = (base - t) / BASE_YRS                      # in/yr
    tp = t - rate * DT_YRS
    b0, b1 = t < CRIT, tp < CRIT
    cross = SURVEY + dt.timedelta(days=(t - CRIT) / rate * YR) if (not b0 and b1) else None
    nxt = SURVEY + dt.timedelta(days=(t - CRIT) / rate * YR) if not b1 else None
    rl0 = None if b0 else (t - CRIT) / rate
    rl1 = None if b1 else (tp - CRIT) / rate
    return dict(t=t, base=base, rate=rate * 1000.0, proj=tp, b0=b0, b1=b1, cross=cross,
                next=nxt, rl0=rl0, rl1=rl1)


ROWS = load_rows()
GRID = [(row, carry(row['rmin'], row['base'])) for row in ROWS]
SCAN = [(row, carry(row['scan'], row['base'])) for row in ROWS if row['scan'] is not None]

# Sensitivity: scan minima carried at the grid-point rate
SENS = []
for row in ROWS:
    if row['scan'] is None:
        continue
    rate = (row['base'] - row['rmin']) / BASE_YRS
    t = row['scan']
    tp = t - rate * DT_YRS
    cross = SURVEY + dt.timedelta(days=(t - CRIT) / rate * YR) if (t >= CRIT and tp < CRIT) else None
    SENS.append((row['grid'], cross))

MEAN0 = statistics.mean([row['rmin'] for row in ROWS])
SD0 = statistics.stdev([row['rmin'] for row in ROWS])
MEAN1 = statistics.mean([p['proj'] for _, p in GRID])
COV = SD0 / MEAN0 * 100.0

IN_SERVICE = dt.date(1980, 9, 5)
LIFE_YRS = (SURVEY - IN_SERVICE).days / YR
NOM_RATE_CE6 = (0.500 - 0.202) / LIFE_YRS * 1000.0


def tmin(H, G, D=92.0, S=23600.0, E=1.0):
    """API 653 4.3.3.1 whole-course minimum thickness (indicative)."""
    return 2.6 * (H - 1.0) * D * G / (S * E)


def level_for(t, G, D=92.0, S=23600.0, E=1.0):
    return t * S * E / (2.6 * D * G) + 1.0


def summary(rows):
    n0 = [x for x in rows if x[1]['b0']]
    n1 = [x for x in rows if x[1]['b1']]
    mn0 = min(rows, key=lambda x: x[1]['t'])
    mn1 = min(rows, key=lambda x: x[1]['proj'])
    cr = sorted([x for x in rows if x[1]['cross']], key=lambda x: x[1]['cross'])
    return dict(n0=n0, n1=n1, mn0=mn0, mn1=mn1, cross=cr)


SUM_GRID = summary(GRID)
SUM_SCAN = summary(SCAN)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    print('elapsed', (TARGET - SURVEY).days, r(DT_YRS, 3))
    for name, rows, s in (('grid', GRID, SUM_GRID), ('scan', SCAN, SUM_SCAN)):
        print(name, len(s['n0']), len(s['n1']), s['mn0'][0]['grid'], r(s['mn0'][1]['t'], 3),
              s['mn1'][0]['grid'], r(s['mn1'][1]['proj'], 3),
              [(x[0]['grid'], d(x[1]['cross'])) for x in s['cross']])
        for row, p in rows:
            print(' ', row['grid'], r(p['t'], 3), r(p['rate'], 2), r(p['proj'], 3), p['b0'], p['b1'],
                  d(p['cross']) if p['cross'] else '', r(p['rl0'], 1) if p['rl0'] is not None else 'nil',
                  r(p['rl1'], 1) if p['rl1'] is not None else 'nil', d(p['next']) if p['next'] else '')
    print('sens', [(g, d(c)) for g, c in SENS if c])
    print('mean0', r(MEAN0, 3), 'COV', r(COV, 1), 'mean1', r(MEAN1, 3))
    print('life', r(LIFE_YRS, 1), 'nominal rate C1-E-6', r(NOM_RATE_CE6, 2))
    for H, G in ((44, 0.96), (44, 0.92), (32, 0.96), (32, 0.92)):
        print('tmin', H, G, r(tmin(H, G), 3), r(tmin(H, G, S=24900), 3))
    print('level for 0.225', r(level_for(0.225, 0.96), 1), r(level_for(0.225, 0.92), 1))

import re
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT, WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

import data as D
from data import r, d

OUT = '/filesystem/T01002_FFS_DISPOSITION.docx'

NAVY = '1F3864'
MID = '2E5597'
ZEBRA = 'F2F5FA'
GROUP = 'D9E2F3'
RED = 'F4CCCC'
AMBER = 'FFE699'
GREEN = 'E2EFDA'
BORDER = 'A6A6A6'
FONT = 'Calibri'

doc = Document()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- styles
st = doc.styles['Normal']
st.font.name = FONT
st.font.size = Pt(10)
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), FONT)
st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08

for name, size, color, before, after in (('Heading 1', 13, NAVY, 12, 4), ('Heading 2', 11, MID, 8, 3),
                                         ('Heading 3', 10, MID, 6, 2)):
    h = doc.styles[name]
    h.font.name = FONT
    h.font.size = Pt(size)
    h.font.bold = True
    h.font.italic = False
    h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    rpr = h.element.get_or_add_rPr()
    rf = rpr.find(qn('w:rFonts'))
    if rf is None:
        rf = OxmlElement('w:rFonts')
        rpr.append(rf)
    for a in ('w:ascii', 'w:hAnsi', 'w:eastAsia', 'w:cs'):
        rf.set(qn(a), FONT)
    for a in ('w:asciiTheme', 'w:hAnsiTheme', 'w:eastAsiaTheme', 'w:cstheme'):
        if rf.get(qn(a)) is not None:
            del rf.attrib[qn(a)]
    h.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    h.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    h.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

lb = doc.styles['List Bullet']
lb.font.name = FONT
lb.font.size = Pt(10)
lb.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
ln = doc.styles['List Number']
ln.font.name = FONT
ln.font.size = Pt(10)
ln.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- page setup
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.page_width, sec.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.8)
sec.top_margin = Inches(0.75)
sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.7)
sec.header_distance = Inches(0.35)
sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.35)


def add_field(run, instr):
    f1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); it.text = instr
    f2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'separate')
    t = OxmlElement('w:t'); t.text = '1'
    f3 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); f3.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    for e in (f1, it, f2, t, f3):
        run._r.append(e)


def set_header_footer(section):
    hp = section.header.paragraphs[0]
    hp.text = ''
    hr = hp.add_run('Turnpike Chemicals LLC — Lake Charles Complex   |   T-01-002 fitness-for-service disposition memo   |   06/15/2026')
    hr.font.size = Pt(8)
    hr.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)
    hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    fp = section.footer.paragraphs[0]
    fp.text = ''
    fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    a = fp.add_run('T01002_FFS_DISPOSITION   |   Record review — not a certified FFS assessment   |   Page ')
    a.font.size = Pt(8); a.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)
    b = fp.add_run(); b.font.size = Pt(8); add_field(b, 'PAGE')
    c = fp.add_run(' of '); c.font.size = Pt(8); c.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)
    e = fp.add_run(); e.font.size = Pt(8); add_field(e, 'NUMPAGES')


set_header_footer(sec)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    for old in tcPr.findall(qn('w:shd')):
        tcPr.remove(old)
    shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
    shd.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'), 'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def rich(par, text, size=None, color=None, bold_all=False, italic=False):
    """Add text to paragraph; **...** marks bold."""
    parts = re.split(r'(\*\*.+?\*\*)', text)
    for p in parts:
        if not p:
            continue
        b = p.startswith('**') and p.endswith('**')
        t = p[2:-2] if b else p
        run = par.add_run(t)
        run.bold = b or bold_all
        run.italic = italic
        if size:
            run.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color:
            run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    return par


def para(text, size=None, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, after=None, before=None, color=None, style=None,
         keep=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else doc.add_paragraph()
    rich(p, text, size=size, color=color, bold_all=bold, italic=italic)
    if align == 'c':
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    elif align == 'j':
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    if after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep:
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p


def bullet(text, size=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet')
    rich(p, text, size=size)
    return p


def numbered(items, size=None):
    """Manual numbering (robust across renderers)."""
    for i, text in enumerate(items, 1):
        p = doc.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
        p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.3)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
        rich(p, f'{i}.\t' + text, size=size)
        p.paragraph_format.tab_stops.add_tab_stop(Inches(0.3))


def caption(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    rich(p, text, size=9, color=NAVY, bold_all=True)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(6)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p


def note(text, size=8.5):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    rich(p, text, size=size, color='404040')
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return p


def table(headers, rows, widths, size=8.5, header_size=8.5, zebra=True, group_rows=(), fills=None,
          bold_first_col=False, align_cols=None, repeat=True):
    """rows: list of lists of str. fills: dict {(ri, ci): hex}. group_rows: indexes of rows rendered as group bars."""
    ncol = len(headers)
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=ncol)
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    tblPr = t._tbl.tblPr
    lay = OxmlElement('w:tblLayout'); lay.set(qn('w:type'), 'fixed'); tblPr.append(lay)
    borders = OxmlElement('w:tblBorders')
    for edge in ('top', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'insideH', 'insideV'):
        el = OxmlElement(f'w:{edge}')
        el.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'), '4'); el.set(qn('w:space'), '0'); el.set(qn('w:color'), BORDER)
        borders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(borders)
    mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
    for side, w in (('top', 25), ('bottom', 25), ('left', 70), ('right', 70)):
        el = OxmlElement(f'w:{side}'); el.set(qn('w:w'), str(w)); el.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); mar.append(el)
    tblPr.append(mar)
    grid = t._tbl.tblGrid
    for i, gc in enumerate(grid.findall(qn('w:gridCol'))):
        gc.set(qn('w:w'), str(int(widths[i] * 1440)))

    def fmt_row(row_cells, values, is_header=False, ri=None, group=False):
        for ci, (cell, val) in enumerate(zip(row_cells, values)):
            cell.width = Inches(widths[ci])
            cell.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER if is_header else WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
            p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
            lines = str(val).split('\n')
            for li, line in enumerate(lines):
                if li > 0:
                    p = cell.add_paragraph()
                    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
                    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
                if is_header:
                    rich(p, line, size=header_size, color='FFFFFF', bold_all=True)
                else:
                    rich(p, line, size=size, bold_all=(group or (bold_first_col and ci == 0)))
                if align_cols and ci in align_cols and not group:
                    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
                if is_header:
                    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER if (align_cols and ci in align_cols) else WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
            if is_header:
                shade(cell, NAVY)
            elif group:
                shade(cell, GROUP)
            elif fills and (ri, ci) in fills:
                shade(cell, fills[(ri, ci)])
            elif zebra and ri % 2 == 1:
                shade(cell, ZEBRA)

    hdr = t.rows[0]
    trPr = hdr._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    if repeat:
        th = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); th.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(th)
    cs = OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); cs.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(cs)
    fmt_row(hdr.cells, headers, is_header=True)
    for ri, values in enumerate(rows):
        row = t.add_row()
        trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
        cs = OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); cs.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(cs)
        if ri in group_rows:
            merged = row.cells[0].merge(row.cells[-1])
            merged.text = ''
            fmt_row([merged], [values[0]], ri=ri, group=True)
            merged.width = Inches(sum(widths))
        else:
            fmt_row(row.cells, values, ri=ri)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t


def box(title, lines, fill='FDECEA', edge='C00000', width=6.9):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)

        el = OxmlElement(f'w:{e}')
        el.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'), '12'); el.set(qn('w:space'), '0'); el.set(qn('w:color'), edge)
        borders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(borders)
    mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
    for side, w in (('top', 90), ('bottom', 90), ('left', 140), ('right', 140)):
        el = OxmlElement(f'w:{side}'); el.set(qn('w:w'), str(w)); el.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); mar.append(el)
    tblPr.append(mar)
    c = t.rows[0].cells[0]
    c.width = Inches(width)
    t._tbl.tblGrid.findall(qn('w:gridCol'))[0].set(qn('w:w'), str(int(width * 1440)))
    shade(c, fill)
    p = c.paragraphs[0]
    rich(p, title, size=11, color=edge, bold_all=True)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    for ln_ in lines:
        q = c.add_paragraph()
        rich(q, ln_, size=10)
        q.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t


def new_section(landscape):
    s = doc.add_section(WD_SECTION.NEW_PAGE)
    if landscape:
        s.orientation = WD_ORIENT.LANDSCAPE
        s.page_width, s.page_height = Inches(11), Inches(8.5)
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(0.6)
        s.top_margin = Inches(0.7)
        s.bottom_margin = Inches(0.6)
    else:
        s.orientation = WD_ORIENT.PORTRAIT
        s.page_width, s.page_height = Inches(8.5), Inches(11)
        s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(0.8)
        s.top_margin = Inches(0.75)
        s.bottom_margin = Inches(0.7)
    return s


# ================================================================ TITLE BLOCK
p = para('TURNPIKE CHEMICALS LLC — LAKE CHARLES COMPLEX', size=9, bold=True, color='595959', after=0)
p = para('MEMORANDUM', size=20, bold=True, color=NAVY, after=2)
p = para('Mechanical Integrity — fitness-for-service record review', size=10, italic=True, color='595959', after=6)

hdr_rows = [
    ['To', 'Steven Lee, Engineering Manager'],
    ['Cc', 'James Merchant, Mechanical Integrity Engineer; Steve David, API 653 Inspector (Cert. No. 653-38472, valid to 02/20/2029); '
           'Leona Cartwright, Engineering Administrator (FFS register)'],
    ['From', 'Mechanical integrity — independent review of the T-01-002 fitness-for-service record'],
    ['Date', '06/15/2026 (record assessed as it stands on this date)'],
    ['Subject', '**T-01-002 (Bund 1, heavy derivative bottoms) — the disposition the fitness-for-service record supports**'],
    ['Record reviewed', 'TC-MECH-FFS-0095 Rev 1, Fitness-for-Service Assessment — T-01-002, issued 11/20/2025 '
                        '(prepared by Merrowfield Inspection Services, LLC; reviewed and accepted by S. David)'],
    ['Governing basis', 'API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 Part 4; API 653; TC-MECH-PROC-0007 Rev 2 (issued 06/03/2026)'],
    ['Appendices', 'A — Course 1 readings by survey basis, carried to 06/15/2026;  B — Check against TC-MECH-PROC-0007 Rev 2 §4;  '
                   'C — Inputs a further assessment needs;  D — Chronology to 06/15/2026'],
    ['Status', 'Record review for Engineering Manager decision. This memo is not itself a fitness-for-service assessment '
               'and carries no API 653 certification.'],
]
t = table(['Memo', ''], hdr_rows, [1.35, 5.55], size=9, header_size=8, zebra=False, bold_first_col=True, repeat=False)
# remove header look of first row: make it a thin navy rule
for c in t.rows[0].cells:
    for pp in c.paragraphs:
        for rr in pp.runs:
            rr.font.size = Pt(1)
t.rows[0].height = Emu(36000)

box('DISPOSITION — NOT FIT FOR CONTINUED SERVICE: REMOVE T-01-002 FROM SERVICE',
    ['On the record as it stands at 06/15/2026, **T-01-002 is not fit for continued service.** Stop receipts, empty and '
     'isolate the tank now, and hold it out of service.',
     'It returns to service only when (1) shell course 1 has been repaired under API 653 Section 9 to a design based on a '

# ================================================================ 1
doc.add_heading('1.  Purpose, scope and conventions', level=1)
para('TC-MECH-FFS-0095 Rev 1 records a minimum measured thickness of 0.196 in on shell course 1 of T-01-002 against an '

doc.add_heading('4.  Why removal from service, and not continued or restricted operation', level=1)
para('Under API 653 a shell course below its acceptance thickness must be repaired, rerated or shown fit by a '
     'fitness-for-service assessment. Here the assessment has been made and shows the tank not fit; there is no rerating '
     'calculation and no repair. Continued operation therefore needs a documented basis, and the record contains none.',
     align='j')
para('Restricted operation at a reduced liquid level is not available on this record. A safe level can only come from a '
     'traceable minimum-thickness calculation, a confirmed specific gravity and plate allowable, and a corrosion allowance '
     'for the restricted period; the record holds none of these in usable form (N2, N3). The indicative check suggests that '
     'even the 32 ft normal operating level needs more wall than course 1 now has on average.', align='j')
para('The loss is active and sits where hoop stress is highest. The 6 in band is losing 10.83–12.67 mpy on the grid basis '
     'and up to 13.67 mpy on the scan basis — about one mil a month — and C1-S-18 reaches the criterion on the grid basis '
     f'on {d([p for row, p in D.GRID if row["grid"] == "C1-S-18"][0]["next"])}, five days after the GPSOA deadline.',
     align='j')
para('Neither the no-shutdown position recorded at the 06/03/2026 and 06/10/2026 meetings nor the Q3 2026 CAPEX window '
     'changes this. GPSOA\'s Notice of Findings says its decision not to issue an imminent-danger order "is not a finding '
     'that continued operation is unconditionally acceptable". The funded repair (TC-MECH-CAP-0047 Rev 1, line 02: four '
     '600 mm × 600 mm patch plates on course 1 and one on course 2) was scoped from the inspection report, not from an '
     'assessment; four patches covering 2.4 m cannot address loss recorded all round the 6 in band of an 88 m circumference. '
     'The turnaround work list (Rev 8, 06/04/2026) carries only a recoat for this tank.', align='j')
para('Emptying the tank makes the empty-tank wind case govern, and that case has not been checked at 70 m/s. The '
     'out-of-service plan should therefore include the empty-tank stability check and, through the hurricane season, any '
     'storm-ballast level, set by calculation (Table 4, actions 1 and 5).', align='j')

[Normal] Under API 653 a shell course below its acceptance thickness must be repaired, rerated or shown fit by a fitness-for-service assessment. [Normal] The negative finding does not rest on the assessment's method. Because TC-MECH-FFS-0095 compares one pit-scan minimum with the criterion instead of following Part 4, its "fail" is not itself a code result, and a profile-based assessment against a 0.225 in minimum could average out the bottom band. But 0.225 in is not a demonstrated minimum: on the record's own fill heights and specific gravity the API 653 minimum is 0.289–0.418 in, and course 1's mean thickness (0.253 in at 06/15/2026) is below the lowest of those. On every thickness basis the record holds, the shell is below a defensible minimum.
[Normal] Restricted operation at a reduced liquid level is not available on this record. A safe level can only come from a traceable minimum-thickness calculation, a confirmed specific gravity and plate allowable, and a corrosion allowance for the restricted period; the record holds none of these in usable form (N2, N3). The indicative check suggests that even the 32 ft normal operating level needs more wall than course 1 now has on average. For the same reason, no Level 2 outcome is likely to support return to service at a useful liquid level without repair, which is why the return-to-service conditions require one.
[Normal] The loss is active and sits where hoop stress is highest. The 6 in band is losing 10.83–12.67 mpy on the grid basis and up to 13.67 mpy on the scan basis — about one mil a month — and C1-S-18 reaches the criterion on the grid basis on 08/15/2026, five days after the GPSOA deadline.
[Normal] Neither the no-shutdown position recorded at the 06/03/2026 and 06/10/2026 meetings nor the Q3 2026 CAPEX window changes this. GPSOA's Notice of Findings says its decision not to issue an imminent-danger order "is not a finding that continued operation is unconditionally acceptable". The funded repair (TC-MECH-CAP-0047 Rev 1, line 02: four 600 mm × 600 mm patch plates on course 1 and one on course 2) was scoped from the inspection report, not from an assessment; four patches covering 2.4 m cannot address loss recorded all round the 6 in band of an 88 m circumference. The turnaround work list (Rev 8, 06/04/2026) carries only a recoat for this tank.
[Normal] Emptying the tank makes the empty-tank wind case govern, and that case has not been checked at 70 m/s. The out-of-service plan should therefore include the empty-tank stability check and, through the hurricane season, any storm-ballast level, set by calculation (Table 4, actions 1 and 5).
[Heading 1] 5.  What I would do before the GPSOA submission
[Normal] The submission must carry a completed, certified FFS file for T-01-002 that states the outcome and the disposition, and a rolling-program entry that matches it. Rev 1 should not be submitted as it stands, and T-01-002 should not appear in the rolling program on a five-year interval.

steps.message:
I've written the memo as `/filesystem/T01002_FFS_DISPOSITION.docx` (15 pages; main memo portrait, appendices landscape). Its disposition is: **T-01-002 is not fit for continued service. Remove it from service now and keep it out until course 1 has been repaired under API 653 §9.** The repair design has to come from a Level 2 assessment that meets TC-MECH-PROC-0007 Rev 2, including a shell-stability check at 70 m/s. The memo asks Steven Lee to sign the decision by 06/19/2026.

**Why the record supports only that disposition**
- **The only assessment on file says "not fit", and nothing has replaced it.** TC-MECH-FFS-0095 Rev 1 (11/20/2025) was validly signed by S. David before his certificate lapsed. Since then there has been no Level 2, repair, rerate, re-survey or Engineering Manager decision. The inspection plan issued two weeks later schedules the next UT survey for 04/2030 as though the tank had passed.
- **The condition is worse at 06/15/2026.** I carried each course 1 grid forward at its own 2019–2025 rate:

| Basis | Below 0.225 in when surveyed (04/11/2025) | Below 0.225 in at 06/15/2026 | Minimum at 06/15/2026 | Grids that crossed in between |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grid reading | 4 of 16 | 5 of 16 | 0.187 in | C1-E-18 on 01/28/2026 |
| Anomaly-scan minimum | 5 of 16 | 8 of 16 | 0.180 in | C1-S-18 06/13/2025, C1-W-18 08/14/2025, C1-N-18 11/19/2025 |

  All four quadrants were already below 0.225 in at the 6 in elevation, so the loss runs all the way round, not at a single pit.
- **The 0.225 in criterion can't be reproduced.** Its calculation sheet isn't on file and the specific gravity and fill height behind it aren't stated. A rough API 653 check using the record's own inputs gives a minimum thickness of 0.289–0.418 in, depending on fill height and specific gravity. The course 1 average (0.253 in at 06/15/2026) is below all of those, so reduced-level operation can't be justified from the record either.
- **The assessment's gaps weaken the file, not the "not fit" finding.** Of the eight inputs the site guidance requires on the face, three are missing (survey reference, corrosion rate, wind basis), three are incomplete and two are mis-cited. Its stability check used the superseded 45 m/s wind speed. Its thickness value is taken from an inspection report that has no API 653 certification.
